sentences.zh: 古者天子娶后，三國來媵，皆有娣侄，凡十二女。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven took a queen, three states sent accompanying brides (ying), each with younger sisters and nieces, twelve women in all.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, when the Son of Heaven took a primary consort, three allied states would each send a ying bride, each accompanied by younger sisters and nieces—twelve women in all.

sentences.zh: 諸侯一娶九女。

translations.literal: Feudal lords in one marriage took nine women.
translations.idiomatic: A feudal lord would take nine wives in a single marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 所以正嫡妾，廣繼嗣，息妒忌，防淫慝，塞禍亂也。

translations.literal: This was in order to regularize primary wife and concubines, extend succession, quell jealousy, guard against debauchery, and block calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose was to fix the hierarchy between primary wife and subordinates, broaden the pool of heirs, calm jealousy, guard against licentious conduct, and forestall disaster and unrest.

sentences.zh: 后亡，則媵為繼室，各以其敘。

translations.literal: When the queen died, then the ying brides became successor wives, each according to her order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: When the primary consort died, the ying brides would become successor wives in order of seniority.

sentences.zh: 無三媵，則娣侄繼室，亦各以其敘。

translations.literal: If there were no three ying brides, then younger sisters and nieces served as successor wives, also each according to her order.
translations.idiomatic: If there were no three ying brides, younger sisters and nieces would fill the role as successor wives, again in order of precedence.

sentences.zh: 繼室者，治其內政，不敢正其位號。

translations.literal: A successor wife administered the inner household but did not dare assume the main title and rank.
translations.idiomatic: A successor wife would run the inner household but would not presume to claim the principal title and rank.

sentences.zh: 禮，廟無兩祔，不並尊也。

translations.literal: By ritual, in a temple there were not two paired shrine tablets; they were not honored on equal footing.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, a temple did not enshrine two consorts of equal standing side by side—dual enshrinement meant treating them as equals.

sentences.zh: 魯成風始兩祔，宋國三媵，齊管氏三歸，《春秋》皆譏之。

translations.literal: In Lu, Cheng Feng was the first to have two paired enshrinements; Song had three ying brides; in Qi, Guan's clan had the Three Returns—all were satirized in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Feng of Lu pioneered double enshrinement, when Song took three ying brides, and when the Guan clan of Qi received the "Three Returns," the Spring and Autumn Annals censured them all.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》內宰，其屬則內小臣、閽人、寺人次之，九嬪、世婦、女御、女祝、女史、典婦功、典絲、典枲、內司服又次之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou lists the Chief Palace Steward; subordinate to her were the Inner Chamberlain, Gatekeepers, and Eunuchs in turn, and below them the Nine Consorts, Palace Matrons, Inner Attendants, Sacrificial Maidens, Palace Scribes, Directors of Women's Work, Directors of Silk, Directors of Hemp, and Inner Director of Garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, the Chief Palace Steward heads the inner administration; beneath her come the Inner Chamberlain, gatekeepers, and eunuchs, and below them the Nine Consorts, palace matrons, inner attendants, sacrificial maidens, palace scribes, directors of women's crafts, silk, and hemp, and the inner director of garments.

sentences.zh: 《昏義》稱「后立六宮、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻」，不與《春秋》、《周禮》合，后世因仍其說，后宮遂至數千。

translations.literal: The Meaning of Marriage states that "the queen established the Six Palaces, three Ladies, nine Consorts, twenty-seven Palace Matrons, and eighty-one Inner Wives," which does not accord with the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Rites of Zhou; later ages followed this account, and the inner palace eventually reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Marriage speaks of the queen establishing the Six Palaces, three Ladies, nine Consorts, twenty-seven palace matrons, and eighty-one inner wives—a scheme that does not match the Spring and Autumn Annals or the Rites of Zhou. Later dynasties kept to this account, and the inner palace eventually swelled to thousands.

sentences.zh: 金代，后不娶庶族，甥舅之家有周姬、齊薑之義。

translations.literal: In the Jin dynasty, the queen was not taken from common clans; marriage with maternal-uncle and paternal-aunt houses had the meaning of the Zhou Ji and Qi Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, primary consorts were not chosen from humble clans; unions with maternal-uncle and paternal-aunt houses carried the same significance as the Zhou princesses and Qi ladies of old.

sentences.zh: 國初諸妃皆無位號，熙宗始有貴妃、賢妃、德妃之號。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state all consorts had no titles; under Emperor Xizong there first appeared the titles Noble Consort, Worthy Consort, and Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early years consorts bore no formal titles; Emperor Xizong was the first to institute Noble, Worthy, and Virtuous Consort ranks.

sentences.zh: 海陵淫嬖，后宮浸多，元妃、姝妃、惠妃、貴妃、賢妃、宸妃、麗妃、淑妃、德妃、昭妃、溫妃、柔妃凡十二位。

translations.literal: Hailing was licentious in favoritism; the inner palace gradually grew, with Primary Consort, Beautiful Consort, Kind Consort, Noble Consort, Worthy Consort, Imperial Consort, Lovely Consort, Pure Consort, Virtuous Consort, Bright Consort, Gentle Consort, and Soft Consort—twelve ranks in all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hailing's indulgence swelled the inner palace to twelve ranks: Primary, Beautiful, Kind, Noble, Worthy, Imperial, Lovely, Pure, Virtuous, Bright, Gentle, and Soft Consort.

sentences.zh: 大定后宮簡少，明昌以后大備。

translations.literal: Under the Dading reign the inner palace was kept sparse; after Mingchang it was fully equipped.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era the inner palace was kept lean; from the Mingchang reign onward it was brought to full establishment.

sentences.zh: 內官制度：諸妃視正一品，比三夫人。

translations.literal: Inner-palace regulations: all consorts were treated as first rank, equivalent to the three Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-palace regulations ranked all consorts at first grade, equivalent to the three Ladies of Zhou ritual.

sentences.zh: 昭儀、昭容、昭媛、修儀、修容、修媛、充儀、充容充媛視正二品，比九嬪。

translations.literal: Bright Lady of Ceremony, Bright Lady of Countenance, Bright Lady of Grace, Cultivated Lady of Ceremony, Cultivated Lady of Countenance, Cultivated Lady of Grace, Fulfilling Lady of Ceremony, Fulfilling Lady of Countenance, and Fulfilling Lady of Grace were treated as second rank, equivalent to the Nine Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright, Cultivated, and Fulfilling Ladies of Ceremony, Countenance, and Grace held second rank, equivalent to the Nine Consorts.

sentences.zh: 婕妤九人視正三品。

translations.literal: Nine Fair Ladies were treated as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Fair Ladies held third rank.

sentences.zh: 美人九人視正四品，才人九人視正五品，比二十七世婦。

translations.literal: Nine Beauties were treated as fourth rank; nine Talented Ladies as fifth rank, equivalent to the twenty-seven Palace Matrons.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Beauties held fourth rank and nine Talented Ladies fifth, equivalent to the twenty-seven palace matrons.

sentences.zh: 寶林二十七人視正六品，御女二十七人視正七品，采女二十七人視正八品，比八十一御妻。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven Treasured Forest Ladies were treated as sixth rank; twenty-seven Inner Maidens as seventh; twenty-seven Selected Maidens as eighth, equivalent to the eighty-one Inner Wives.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven Treasured Forest Ladies held sixth rank, twenty-seven Inner Maidens seventh, and twenty-seven Selected Maidens eighth—equivalent to the eighty-one inner wives.

sentences.zh: 又有尚宮、尚儀、尚服、尚食、尚寢、尚功，皆內官也。

translations.literal: There were also the Chief of Palace, Chief of Ceremonies, Chief of Wardrobe, Chief of Provisions, Chief of Quarters, and Chief of Works—all inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Chiefs of Palace, Ceremonies, Wardrobe, Provisions, Quarters, and Works—all inner-palace offices.

sentences.zh: 太祖嫡后聖穆生景宣，光懿生宗幹，有定策功，欽憲有保佑之功，故自熙宗時聖穆、光懿、欽憲皆祔。

translations.literal: Taizu's primary consort Shengmu bore Jingxuan; Guangyi bore Zonggan, who had the merit of settling the succession; Qinxian had the merit of protection—therefore from Xizong's time Shengmu, Guangyi, and Qinxian were all enshrined alongside him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's primary consort Shengmu bore Jingxuan; Guangyi bore Zonggan, who had settled the succession; Qinxian had protected the house—so from Emperor Xizong onward Shengmu, Guangyi, and Qinxian were all enshrined in Taizu's temple.

sentences.zh: 宣獻生睿宗，大定祔焉。

translations.literal: Xuanxian bore Ruizong; under Dading she was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanxian bore Emperor Ruizong and was enshrined in his temple during the Dading reign.

sentences.zh: 故太祖廟祔四后，睿、世、顯、宣皆祔兩后，惟太宗、景宣、熙宗、章宗室祔一后。

translations.literal: Therefore in Taizu's temple four consorts were enshrined; Ruizong, Shizong, Xianzong, and Xuanzong each had two consorts enshrined; only Taizong, Jingxuan, Xizong, and Zhangzong's shrines had one consort enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's temple thus enshrined four consorts; the temples of Ruizong, Shizong, Xianzong, and Xuanzong each enshrined two, while only Taizong, Jingxuan, Xizong, and Zhangzong enshrined a single consort.

sentences.zh: 貞、慈、光獻、昭聖雖庶姓，皆以子貴。

translations.literal: Zhen, Ci, Guangxian, and Zhaosheng, though of common clans, all rose in honor through their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts Zhen, Ci, Guangxian, and Zhaosheng were of humble birth, yet each was elevated through her son's eminence.

sentences.zh: 宣宗冊溫敦氏，乃賜姓，變古甚矣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong enfeoffed the Wendun clan, which was a granted surname—a great departure from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ennobled the Wendun clan—a bestowed surname and a striking break with ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 故自初起至於國亡，列其世次，著其族裏，可考鑒焉。

translations.literal: Therefore from the first rise to the fall of the state, their generations are arrayed and their clans and villages recorded, so that one may examine and reflect.
translations.idiomatic: From the dynasty's rise to its fall, their generations, clans, and homelands are set forth here for examination and reflection.

sentences.zh: 其無與于世道者，置不錄。

translations.literal: Those who had no bearing on the way of the world are omitted and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had no bearing on affairs of state are omitted.

sentences.zh: 始祖明懿皇后

translations.literal: Founding Ancestor's Empress Mingyi
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mingyi, Consort of the Founding Ancestor

sentences.zh: 始祖明懿皇后，完顏部人。

translations.literal: Founding Ancestor's Empress Mingyi was of the Wanyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mingyi of the Founding Ancestor was a woman of the Wanyan clan.

sentences.zh: 年六十餘嫁始祖。

translations.literal: At over sixty years of age she married the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: She was over sixty when she married the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 德帝思皇后

translations.literal: Empress Si, Consort of Emperor De
translations.idiomatic: Empress Si, Consort of Emperor De

sentences.zh: 德帝思皇后，不知何部人。

translations.literal: Empress Si, Consort of Emperor De—it is not known of which clan she was.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Si, consort of Emperor De—her clan is unknown.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 安帝節皇后

translations.literal: Empress Jie, Consort of Emperor An
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jie, Consort of Emperor An

sentences.zh: 安帝節皇后，不知何部人。

translations.literal: Empress Jie, Consort of Emperor An—it is not known of which clan she was.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jie, consort of Emperor An—her clan is unknown.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 獻祖恭靖皇后

translations.literal: Empress Gongjing, Consort of Xianzu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongjing, Consort of Xianzu

sentences.zh: 獻祖恭靖皇后，不知何部人。

translations.literal: Empress Gongjing, Consort of Xianzu—it is not known of which clan she was.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongjing, consort of Xianzu—her clan is unknown.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 昭祖威順皇后

translations.literal: Empress Weishun, Consort of Zhaozu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Weishun, Consort of Zhaozu

sentences.zh: 昭祖威順皇后徒單氏，諱烏古論都葛，活刺渾水敵魯鄉徒單部人。

translations.literal: Empress Weishun of Zhaozu was of the Tudian clan; her taboo name was Wugulun Duge; she was a woman of the Tudian clan of Dielu village on the Huocihun River.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Weishun of Zhaozu, née Tudian, taboo name Wugulun Duge, came from the Tudian clan of Dielu village on the Huocihun River.

sentences.zh: 其父拔炭都魯海。

translations.literal: Her father was Batanduluhai.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Batanduluhai.

sentences.zh: 后性剛毅，人莫敢以為室。

translations.literal: The consort's nature was firm and resolute; no one dared take her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: She was so firm and resolute in character that no man dared marry her.

sentences.zh: 獻祖將為昭祖娶婦，曰：「此子勇斷異常，柔弱之女不可以為配。」

translations.literal: Xianzu was about to take a wife for Zhaozu and said: "This son is exceptionally brave and decisive; a weak and yielding woman cannot be matched to him."
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu was choosing a wife for Zhaozu, he said, "This son is unusually bold and decisive—a timid, yielding woman would not suit him."

sentences.zh: 乃為昭祖娶焉。

translations.literal: So he took her in marriage for Zhaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave her to Zhaozu in marriage.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 景祖昭肅皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosu, Consort of Jingzu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosu, Consort of Jingzu

sentences.zh: 景祖昭肅皇后，唐括氏，帥水隈鴉村唐括部人，諱多保真。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosu of Jingzu was of the Tangkuo clan, a woman of the Tangkuo clan of Yacun on the Shuai River; her taboo name was Duobaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosu of Jingzu, née Tangkuo, came from the Tangkuo clan of Yacun on the Shuai River; her taboo name was Duobaozhen.

sentences.zh: 父石批德撒骨只，巫者也。

translations.literal: Her father Shipide Saguji was a shaman.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shipide Saguji was a shaman.

sentences.zh: 后有識度，在父母家好待賓客，父母出，則多置酒饌享鄰里，迨於行旅。

translations.literal: The consort had discernment and breadth; in her parents' home she was fond of entertaining guests. When her parents went out, she would set out much food and drink to feast the neighbors, extending even to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was discerning and magnanimous. In her parents' home she delighted in receiving guests; when they were away she would lay out food and drink for neighbors and travelers alike.

sentences.zh: 景祖飲食過人，時人名之「活羅」，解在《景祖紀》。

translations.literal: Jingzu ate and drank beyond ordinary men; people of the time called him "Huoluo"; the explanation is in the Basic Annals of Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu ate and drank more than other men; people of the time nicknamed him "Huoluo"—the explanation appears in his Basic Annals.

sentences.zh: 昭祖曰：「儉嗇之女吝惜酒食，不可以配。」

translations.literal: Zhaozu said: "A frugal and stingy woman who begrudges food and drink cannot be matched to him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu said, "A miserly woman who grudges food and drink would not suit him."

sentences.zh: 烏古乃聞后性度如是，乃娶焉。

translations.literal: Wugunai heard that the consort's character and breadth were such, and took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Wugunai heard that the consort's character matched this need, he took her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 遼使同幹來伐五國浦聶部，景祖使后與劾孫為質于拔乙門，而與同幹襲取之，遼主以景祖為節度使。

translations.literal: A Liao envoy, Tonggan, came to attack the Ponie tribe of the Five States; Jingzu sent the consort and Helsun as hostages to Bayimen, then joined with Tonggan in a surprise attack to take it; the Liao sovereign made Jingzu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao envoy Tonggan came to attack the Ponie tribe of the Five States, Jingzu sent the consort and Helsun as hostages to Bayimen, then joined Tonggan in a surprise attack to seize the place; the Liao emperor appointed Jingzu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 后雖喜賓客，而自不飲酒。

translations.literal: Though the consort delighted in guests, she herself did not drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: Though she delighted in entertaining guests, she never drank wine herself.

sentences.zh: 景祖與客飲，后專聽之。

translations.literal: When Jingzu drank with guests, the consort listened intently.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzu drank with his guests, the consort listened closely to everything said.

sentences.zh: 翌日，枚數其人所為，無一不中其啟肯。

translations.literal: The next day she would enumerate each person's conduct, and not one failed to match what was in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she would recount each man's words and deeds, and never missed what was truly in his mind.

sentences.zh: 有醉而喧呶者，輒自歌以釋其忿爭。

translations.literal: When someone was drunk and clamorous, she would herself sing to release their angry quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: When guests grew drunk and quarrelsome, she would sing herself to calm their anger.

sentences.zh: 軍中有被笞罰者，每以酒食慰諭之。

translations.literal: When men in the army had been flogged and punished, she would each time comfort and instruct them with food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who had been flogged she would comfort with food and drink.

sentences.zh: 景祖行部，輒與偕行，政事獄訟皆與決焉。

translations.literal: When Jingzu toured the districts, she always went with him; government affairs and lawsuits were all decided with her.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jingzu toured his districts she accompanied him, and all government business and lawsuits were decided with her counsel.

sentences.zh: 景祖沒後，世祖兄弟凡用兵，皆稟於后而后行，勝負皆有懲勸。

translations.literal: After Jingzu's death, whenever Shizu's brothers undertook military action they all reported to the consort before acting; victory and defeat each brought reward or admonition.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzu died, Shizu and his brothers would consult the consort before every campaign; whether they won or lost, she rewarded or admonished them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 農月，親課耕耘刈獲，遠則乘馬，近則策杖，勤於事者勉之，晏出早休者訓勵之。

translations.literal: In the farming months she personally inspected plowing, sowing, reaping, and harvesting; for distant fields she rode a horse, for near ones she used a staff; those diligent in their work she encouraged, those who went out late and rested early she instructed and urged.
translations.idiomatic: During the farming season she personally inspected plowing and harvest; she rode for distant fields and walked with a staff for nearby ones, encouraging the diligent and reproving those who started late and quit early.

sentences.zh: 后往邑屯村，世祖、肅宗皆從。

translations.literal: When the consort went to Yitun village, Shizu and Suzong both followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort visited Yitun village, Shizu and Suzong accompanied her.

sentences.zh: 會桓赧、散達偕來，是時已有隙，被酒，語相侵不能平，遂舉刃相向。

translations.literal: It happened that Huan'an and Sanda came together; at that time there was already a rift; they were drunk, their words insulted each other and could not be settled, and they drew blades against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Huan'an and Sanda arrived together; old grievances still rankled, and once drunk their words turned insulting until neither could yield, and they drew blades on each other.

sentences.zh: 后起，兩執其手，謂桓赧、散達曰：「汝等皆吾夫時舊人，奈何一旦遽忘吾夫之恩，與小兒子輩忿爭乎。」

translations.literal: The consort rose, seized both their hands, and said to Huan'an and Sanda: "You are all old companions from my husband's time—how can you in a single day so quickly forget my husband's kindness and quarrel in anger with these young men?"
translations.idiomatic: The consort rose and seized both men's hands. "You were all my husband's old companions," she told Huan'an and Sanda. "How can you forget his kindness overnight and quarrel with these young men?"

sentences.zh: 因自作歌，桓赧、散達怒乃解。

translations.literal: Then she herself composed a song, and Huan'an and Sanda's anger was released.
translations.idiomatic: She then sang a song of her own composition, and Huan'an and Sanda's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 其後桓赧兄弟起兵來攻，當是時，肅宗先已再失利矣，世祖已退烏春兵，與桓赧戰於北隘甸。

translations.literal: Afterward Huan'an's brothers raised troops and came to attack; at that time Suzong had already twice been defeated, Shizu had already repelled Wuchun's army, and fought Huan'an at Beiaidian.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huan'an's brothers raised troops to attack. By then Suzong had already suffered two defeats, while Shizu had repelled Wuchun's forces and was fighting Huan'an at Beiaidian.

sentences.zh: 部人失束寬逃歸，袒甲而至，告曰：「軍敗矣。」

translations.literal: A tribesman, Shikuang, fled back; he came bare-chested in armor and reported: "The army is defeated."
translations.idiomatic: A tribesman named Shikuang fled back, his armor stripped to the chest, and cried, "The army is defeated!"

sentences.zh: 后方憂懣，會康宗來報捷，后乃喜。

translations.literal: The consort was then worried and distressed; it happened that Kangzong came with news of victory, and the consort was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was stricken with worry until Kangzong arrived with news of victory, and only then did she rejoice.

sentences.zh: 既而桓赧、散達皆降。

translations.literal: Before long Huan'an and Sanda both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huan'an and Sanda both submitted.

sentences.zh: 后不妒忌，闊略女工，能輯睦宗族，當時以為有丈夫之度云。

translations.literal: The consort was not jealous; she was broad and indifferent to women's crafts; she could harmonize the clan—people of the time thought she had a man's breadth, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: She was free of jealousy, cared little for women's needlework, and could unite the clan; people of the day said she had the bearing of a man.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 世祖翼簡皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yijian, Consort of Shizu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yijian, Consort of Shizu

sentences.zh: 世祖翼簡皇后，拿懶氏。

translations.literal: Empress Yijian of Shizu was of the Nalan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yijian of Shizu was of the Nalan clan.

sentences.zh: 大安元年癸酉歲卒。

translations.literal: She died in the year guiyou of the first year of Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the guiyou year, the first year of the Da'an era.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 肅宗靖宣皇后

translations.literal: Empress Jingxuan, Consort of Suzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jingxuan, Consort of Suzong

sentences.zh: 肅宗靖宣皇后，蒲察氏。

translations.literal: Empress Jingxuan of Suzong was of the Pucha clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jingxuan of Suzong was of the Pucha clan.

sentences.zh: 太祖將舉兵，入告於后。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to raise troops, he went in to inform the consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was about to take the field, he went in to tell the consort.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「汝邦家之長，見可則行。

translations.literal: The consort said: "You are the head of the state and clan; when you see the opportunity, act.
translations.idiomatic: The consort said, "You are head of house and state—when you see your chance, act.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣，無貽我憂，汝亦必不至是。」

translations.literal: I am old; do not leave me worry—and you surely will not come to that."
translations.idiomatic: I am old; do not burden me with worry—and you surely will not bring me to grief."

sentences.zh: 太祖奉觴為壽，即奉后出門，驩酒禱天。

translations.literal: Taizu raised a cup to wish her long life, then escorted the consort out the gate, made merry with wine, and prayed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raised a cup to wish her long life, then led the consort outside, drank in celebration, and prayed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 后命太祖正坐，號令諸將。

translations.literal: The consort ordered Taizu to sit upright and command the generals.
translations.idiomatic: The consort had Taizu take the seat of command and issue orders to the generals.

sentences.zh: 自是太祖每出師還，輒率諸將上謁，獻所俘獲。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever Taizu returned from campaign he would lead the generals to pay respects and present what had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever Taizu returned from campaign he would lead the generals to pay his respects and present the spoils of war.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 穆宗貞惠皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhenhui, Consort of Muzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenhui, Consort of Muzong

sentences.zh: 穆宗貞惠皇后，烏古論氏。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenhui of Muzong was of the Wugulun clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenhui of Muzong was of the Wugulun clan.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 康宗敬僖皇后

translations.literal: Empress Jingxi, Consort of Kangzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jingxi, Consort of Kangzong

sentences.zh: 康宗敬僖皇后，唐括氏。

translations.literal: Empress Jingxi of Kangzong was of the Tangkuo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jingxi of Kangzong was of the Tangkuo clan.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后

translations.literal: Empress Shengmu, Consort of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shengmu, Consort of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后，唐括氏。

translations.literal: Empress Shengmu of Taizu was of the Tangkuo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shengmu of Taizu was of the Tangkuo clan.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年追諡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the thirteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 仍贈后父留速太尉、榮國公，祖迭胡本司徒、英國公，曾禱劾乃司空、溫國公。

translations.literal: Her father's post was also granted: Liusu as Grand Marshal and Duke of Rong; her grandfather Diehuben as Minister of Works and Duke of Ying; her great-grandfather Daojienai as Minister of Works and Duke of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Liusu was also enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and Duke of Rong; her grandfather Diehuben as Minister of Works and Duke of Ying; and her great-grandfather Daojienai as Minister of Works and Duke of Wen.

sentences.zh: 太祖光懿皇后

translations.literal: Empress Guangyi, Consort of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guangyi, Consort of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖光懿皇后，裴滿氏。

translations.literal: Empress Guangyi of Taizu was of the Peiman clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guangyi of Taizu was of the Peiman clan.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年追諡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the thirteenth year of the Tianhui reign.

sentences.zh: 太祖欽憲皇后

translations.literal: Empress Qinxian, Consort of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinxian, Consort of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖欽憲皇后，紇石烈氏。

translations.literal: Empress Qinxian of Taizu was of the Hesheli clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinxian of Taizu was of the Hesheli clan.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年，尊為太皇太后，宮號慶元。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager; her palace was named Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Tianhui reign she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, with the palace name Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月己巳朔，熙宗朝于慶元宮，然後御乾元殿，受群臣賀。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the first day of the first month, the day jisi, Xizong paid court at Qingyuan Palace, then proceeded to Qianyuan Hall and received congratulations from the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the first day of the first month in the fourteenth year, Emperor Xizong paid his respects at Qingyuan Palace, then took the throne at Qianyuan Hall to receive congratulations from the ministers.

sentences.zh: 是月丁丑，崩于慶元宮。

translations.literal: That month on the day dingchou she died at Qingyuan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, on dingchou day, she died at Qingyuan Palace.

sentences.zh: 二月癸卯，祔葬睿陵。

translations.literal: In the second month on the day guimao she was enshrined and buried at Ruiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guimao day, she was enshrined and buried at Ruiling.

sentences.zh: 太祖宣獻皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxian, Consort of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxian, Consort of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖宣獻皇后，僕散氏，睿宗母也。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxian of Taizu was of the Pusan clan; she was Ruizong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxian of Taizu, née Pusan, was the mother of Emperor Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年，追冊曰德妃。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui she was posthumously enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Tianhui reign she was posthumously enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 大定元年追諡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading she was posthumously enfeoffed with a title.
translations.idiomatic: She received her posthumous title in the first year of the Dading reign.

sentences.zh: 太祖崇妃蕭氏

translations.literal: Chongfei Xiaoshi, Consort of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Chongfei Xiaoshi, Consort of Taizu

sentences.zh: 崇妃，蕭氏。

translations.literal: Chongfei was of the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongfei was a woman of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 熙宗時封貴妃。

translations.literal: Under Xizong she was enfeoffed as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong she was made Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 天德二年正月，封元妃。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiande she was enfeoffed as Primary Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of the Tiande reign she was made Primary Consort.

sentences.zh: 是月，尊封太妃。

translations.literal: That month she was honored and enfeoffed as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: That same month she was honored as Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 海陵母大氏事蕭氏甚謹。

translations.literal: Hailing's mother, the Dashis, served the Xiaos with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's mother, Lady Da, served Chongfei Xiao with scrupulous deference.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，尊大氏為皇太后，居永甯宮。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, he honored the Dashis as Empress Dowager, dwelling at Yongning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing seized the throne, he honored Lady Da as Empress Dowager and installed her at Yongning Palace.

sentences.zh: 每有宴集，太妃坐上坐，大氏執婦禮。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a banquet, the Grand Consort sat in the seat of honor and the Dashis performed the rites of a daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the Grand Consort took the seat of honor while Lady Da performed the rites due a daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 海陵積不能平，及殺宗義等，誣太妃以隱惡，殺之，並殺所生子任王隈喝。

translations.literal: Hailing's resentment could not be settled; when he killed Zongyi and others, he falsely accused the Grand Consort of concealing evil and killed her, also killing her son, Prince Ren Wuneihe.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's resentment festered until, after killing Zongyi and others, he falsely accused the Grand Consort of concealing wrongdoing, put her to death, and killed her son Prince Ren Wuneihe as well.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年，詔改葬。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading an edict ordered reburial.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Dading reign an edict ordered her reburial.

sentences.zh: 大宗正丞宗安監護葬事，遣使致祭。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Zong'an supervised the burial; envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Zong'an supervised the burial, and envoys were sent to perform the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上欲復太妃舊號，下禮官議。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to restore the Grand Consort's former title and referred the matter to the ritual officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to restore her former title as Grand Consort and referred the matter to the ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 「前代稱太妃者皆以子貴。

translations.literal: "In former ages those called Grand Consort were all honored through their sons.
translations.idiomatic: "In former ages the title Grand Consort was conferred only when a son had risen to eminence.

sentences.zh: 古者入廟稱『后』係夫，在朝稱『太』係子，與今蕭妃事不同，恐不得稱『太』，止當追封妃號。」

translations.literal: In antiquity, entering the temple one was called 'empress' in relation to the husband; at court one was called 'grand' in relation to the son—this differs from Consort Xiao's case today; I fear she cannot be called 'grand,' and should only be posthumously enfeoffed with a consort's title."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity 'empress' in the ancestral temple referred to the husband, and 'grand' at court referred to the son—Consort Xiao's case differs, and she probably cannot be called 'grand'; she should receive only a posthumous consort title."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，乃封崇妃云。

translations.literal: An edict followed this advice, and she was enfeoffed as Chongfei.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed this advice, and she was posthumously enfeoffed as Chongfei.

sentences.zh: 太宗欽仁皇后

translations.literal: Empress Qinren, Consort of Taizong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinren, Consort of Taizong

sentences.zh: 熙宗悼平皇后

translations.literal: Empress Daoping, Consort of Xizong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Daoping, Consort of Xizong

sentences.zh: 熙宗悼平皇后，裴滿氏。

translations.literal: Empress Daoping of Xizong was of the Peiman clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Daoping of Xizong was of the Peiman clan.

sentences.zh: 熙宗即位，封貴妃。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, she was enfeoffed as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong ascended the throne, she was made Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianjuan reign she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 父忽達拜太尉，贈曾祖斜也司空，祖鶻沙司徒。

translations.literal: Her father Huda was appointed Grand Marshal; her great-grandfather Xieye was posthumously granted Minister of Works; her grandfather Husha was granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Huda was appointed Grand Marshal; her great-grandfather Xieye was posthumously made Minister of Works; her grandfather Husha was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，熙宗受尊號，冊為慈明恭孝順德皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangtong, when Xizong received his honorific title, she was enfeoffed as Empress Ciming Gongxiao Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Huangtong reign, when Xizong received his honorific title, she was enfeoffed as Empress Ciming Gongxiao Shunde.

sentences.zh: 二年，太子濟安生。

translations.literal: In the second year the crown prince Ji'an was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Crown Prince Ji'an was born.

sentences.zh: 是歲，熙宗年二十四，喜甚，乃肆赦，告天地宗廟。

translations.literal: That year Xizong was twenty-four; he was exceedingly pleased and proclaimed a general amnesty, reporting to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xizong was twenty-four; overjoyed, he proclaimed a general amnesty and reported the birth to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 彌月，冊為皇太子，未一歲薨。

translations.literal: At the completion of his first month he was enfeoffed as crown prince; before one year had passed he died.
translations.idiomatic: At his first-month ceremony he was installed as crown prince, but died before he was a year old.

sentences.zh: 久之，熙宗積怒，遂殺后，而納胙王常勝妃撒卯入宮繼之。

translations.literal: After a long while Xizong's anger accumulated, and he killed the empress, then took Prince Zuo Changsheng's consort Samao into the palace to succeed her.
translations.idiomatic: In time Xizong's anger boiled over; he killed the empress and brought Prince Zuo Changsheng's consort Samao into the palace to take her place.

sentences.zh: 又殺德妃烏古論氏，妃夾谷氏、張氏、裴滿氏。

translations.literal: He also killed Virtuous Consort of the Wugulun clan, and consorts of the Jiagu, Zhang, and Peiman clans.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Virtuous Consort Wugulun and consorts of the Jiagu, Zhang, and Peiman clans.

sentences.zh: 明日，熙宗遇弑。

translations.literal: The next day Xizong was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xizong was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 海陵已弑熙宗，欲收人心，以后死無罪，降熙宗為東昏王，追諡后為悼皇后，封后父忽達為王。

translations.literal: Hailing had already assassinated Xizong and wished to win hearts; because the empress's death was without guilt, he demoted Xizong to Prince Donghun, posthumously enfeoffed the empress as Empress Dao, and enfeoffed her father Huda as prince.
translations.idiomatic: After assassinating Xizong, Hailing sought to win popular favor: declaring the empress guiltless in death, he demoted Xizong to Prince Donghun, gave the empress the posthumous title Empress Dao, and enfeoffed her father Huda as a prince.

sentences.zh: 大定間，復熙宗帝號，加諡后為悼平皇后，祔葬思陵。

translations.literal: During Dading, Xizong's imperial title was restored; the empress was given the additional posthumous title Empress Daoping and enshrined at Siling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era Xizong's imperial title was restored, the empress was given the fuller posthumous title Empress Daoping, and she was enshrined at Siling.

sentences.zh: 海陵嫡母徒單氏

translations.literal: Hailing's Primary Mother, the Tudans
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's Primary Mother, Lady Tudian

sentences.zh: 海陵嫡母，徒單氏。

translations.literal: Hailing's primary mother was of the Tudian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's primary mother was of the Tudian clan.

sentences.zh: 宗幹之正室也。

translations.literal: She was Zonggan's principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: She was the principal wife of Zonggan.

sentences.zh: 徒單無子，次室李氏生長子鄭王充，次室大氏生三子，長即海陵庶人也。

translations.literal: Tudian had no sons; the second wife, the Lis, bore the eldest son Prince Zheng Chong; the second wife, the Dashis, bore three sons—the eldest being Hailing the commoner-born.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian had no sons of her own; the second wife, Lady Li, bore the eldest son Prince Zheng Chong; the second wife, Lady Da, bore three sons, the eldest being Hailing, born of a secondary wife.

sentences.zh: 徒單氏賢，遇下有恩意，大氏事之甚謹，相得歡甚。

translations.literal: The Tudans were worthy; in dealing with subordinates they showed kindness, and the Dashis served them with great deference—they got on in great harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian was virtuous and gracious to those below her; Lady Da served her with scrupulous deference, and the two lived together in great harmony.

sentences.zh: 徒單雖養充為己子，充與海陵俱為熙宗宰相，充嗜酒，徒單常責怒之，尤愛海陵。

translations.literal: Though Tudian raised Chong as her own son, Chong and Hailing were both Xizong's chief ministers; Chong was fond of wine, and Tudian often scolded him in anger, but especially loved Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lady Tudian had raised Chong as her own son, both Chong and Hailing served as Xizong's chief ministers; Chong was a heavy drinker and she often scolded him, yet she especially favored Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵自以其母大氏與徒單嫡妾之分，心常不安。

translations.literal: Hailing himself, because his mother the Dashis and Tudian were distinguished as principal wife and concubine, was constantly uneasy in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing himself was constantly uneasy, knowing his mother Lady Da was only a secondary wife while Lady Tudian was the principal consort.

sentences.zh: 及弑熙宗，徒單與太祖妃蕭氏聞之，相顧愕然曰：「帝雖失道，人臣豈可至此。」

translations.literal: When Xizong was assassinated, Tudian and Taizu's consort the Xiaos heard of it; they looked at each other in shock and said: "Though the emperor lost the Way, how can a subject go so far?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong was assassinated, Lady Tudian and Taizu's consort Xiao looked at each other in shock and said, "The emperor may have lost the Way, but how can a subject go this far?"

sentences.zh: 徒單入宮見海陵，不曾賀，海陵銜之。

translations.literal: Tudian entered the palace to see Hailing and did not offer congratulations; Hailing harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian went into the palace to see Hailing but offered no congratulations, and Hailing bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 天德二年正月，徒單與大氏俱尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiande, Tudian and the Dashis were both honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of the Tiande reign, both Lady Tudian and Lady Da were honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 徒單居東宮，號永壽宮，大氏居西宮，號永甯宮。

translations.literal: Tudian dwelt in the Eastern Palace, called Yongshou Palace; the Dashis dwelt in the Western Palace, called Yongning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian lived in the Eastern Palace, known as Yongshou Palace; Lady Da lived in the Western Palace, known as Yongning Palace.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，太后父蒲帶與大氏父俱贈太尉，封王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, the empress dowagers' fathers Pudai and the Dashis' father were both posthumously granted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tiande reign, Empress Dowager Tudian's father Pudai and Lady Da's father were both posthumously made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 徒單太后生日，酒酣，大氏起為壽。

translations.literal: On Empress Dowager Tudian's birthday, when the wine was deep, the Dashis rose to offer a toast for long life.
translations.idiomatic: On Empress Dowager Tudian's birthday, when the wine had flowed freely, Lady Da rose to offer a toast for long life.

sentences.zh: 徒單方與坐客語，大氏跽者久之。

translations.literal: Tudian was conversing with seated guests; the Dashis knelt for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian was talking with the seated guests while Lady Da knelt for a long time.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒而出。

translations.literal: Hailing left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing stormed out in anger.

sentences.zh: 明日，召諸公主宗婦與太后語者皆杖之。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned all princesses and clan wives who had spoken with the empress dowager and had them beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned every princess and clan wife who had spoken with the empress dowager and had them beaten.

sentences.zh: 大氏以為不可。

translations.literal: The Dashis said this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da protested that this should not be done.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「今日之事，豈能尚如前日邪。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Today's affairs—how can they still be as in former days?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "How can affairs today still be as they were in former days?"

sentences.zh: 自是嫌隙愈深。

translations.literal: From then on mutual resentment grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rift between them grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 天德四年，海陵遷中都，獨留徒單于上京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiande, Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, leaving Tudian alone at Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Tiande reign Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, leaving Lady Tudian alone at Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 徒單常憂懼，每中使至，必易衣以俟命。

translations.literal: Tudian was constantly worried and fearful; whenever an imperial messenger arrived, she would change clothes to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian lived in constant fear; whenever an imperial messenger arrived, she would change her clothes to await his command.

sentences.zh: 大氏在中都常思念徒單太后，謂海陵曰：「永壽宮待吾母子甚厚，慎毋相忘也。」

translations.literal: The Dashis at Zhongdu often missed Empress Dowager Tudian and said to Hailing: "Yongshou Palace treated my son and me with great kindness—take care not to forget her."
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongdu Lady Da often missed Empress Dowager Tudian and told Hailing, "Yongshou Palace treated my son and me with great kindness—be sure you do not forget her."

sentences.zh: 十二月十四日，徒單氏生日，海陵使秘書監納合椿年往上京為太后上壽。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, Tudian's birthday, Hailing sent Secretariat Director Nahan Chunnian to Shangjing to offer the empress dowager birthday congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, Lady Tudian's birthday, Hailing sent Secretariat Director Nahan Chunnian to Shangjing to offer her birthday congratulations.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，大氏病篤，恨不得一見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan the Dashis were gravely ill and bitterly wished for one meeting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenyuan reign Lady Da fell gravely ill and longed bitterly for one last meeting.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂海陵曰：「汝以我之故，不令永壽宮偕來中都。

translations.literal: On her deathbed she said to Hailing: "Because of me you did not let Yongshou Palace come together to Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she told Hailing, "Because of me you would not let Yongshou Palace come to Zhongdu with us.

sentences.zh: 我死，必迎致之，事永壽宮當如事我。」

translations.literal: When I die, you must bring her here; serve Yongshou Palace as you would serve me."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you must bring her here and serve Yongshou Palace as you would serve me."

sentences.zh: 三年，右丞相僕散師恭、大宗正丞胡拔魯往上京奉遷山陵，海陵因命永壽宮太后與俱來。

translations.literal: In the third year, Right Chancellor Pusan Shigong and Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Hubalu went to Shangjing to escort the imperial tombs in relocation; Hailing therefore ordered the Yongshou Palace empress dowager to come with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Right Chancellor Pusan Shigong and Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Hubalu went to Shangjing to relocate the imperial tombs, and Hailing ordered the Yongshou Palace empress dowager to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 繼使平章政事蕭玉迎祭祖宗梓宮于廣寧，海陵謂玉曰：「醫巫閭山多佳致。

translations.literal: He then sent Grand Councilor Xiao Yu to welcome and sacrifice to the ancestral coffins at Guangning; Hailing told Yu: "Mount Yiwulü has many fine views.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Grand Councilor Xiao Yu to Guangning to receive and sacrifice before the ancestral coffins. Hailing told Yu, "Mount Yiwulü has many fine vistas.

sentences.zh: 祭奠禮畢，可奏太后于山水佳處遊覽。」

translations.literal: When the sacrificial rites are complete, you may report to the empress dowager to tour places of fine mountains and waters."
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifices are finished, invite the empress dowager to tour the finest scenic spots."

sentences.zh: 及至沙流河，海陵迎謁梓宮，遂謁見太后。

translations.literal: When they reached the Shaliu River, Hailing went out to welcome and pay respects to the coffins, then paid court to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Shaliu River, Hailing went out to receive the coffins and then paid his respects to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 海陵命左右約杖二束自隨，跪于太后前，謝罪曰：「亮不孝，久闕溫靖，願太后痛笞之。

translations.literal: Hailing ordered his attendants to bring two bundles of binding rods; kneeling before the empress dowager he apologized: "Liang is unfilial; for long I have lacked warm attendance—may the empress dowager beat me severely.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered his attendants to bring two bundles of rods, knelt before the empress dowager, and said, "Liang has been unfilial and long neglected you—please beat me severely.

sentences.zh: 不然，且不安。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I cannot be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I cannot rest easy."

sentences.zh: 太后親扶起之，叱約杖者使去。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally helped him up and shouted at those with the binding rods to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager helped him up herself and ordered the attendants with the rods to leave.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「今庶民有克家子，立百金之產，尚且愛之不忍笞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Today common people who have a son who can manage the household and establish a fortune of a hundred gold still love him and cannot bear to beat him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Even common folk who have a son who can manage the household and build a fortune of a hundred gold still love him too much to beat him.

sentences.zh: 我有子如此，寧忍笞乎。」

translations.literal: I have a son such as this—how could I bear to beat him?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I bear to beat a son such as this?"

sentences.zh: 十月，太后至中都，海陵帥百官郊迎，入居壽康宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the empress dowager reached Zhongdu; Hailing led the hundred officials to welcome her at the suburbs, and she entered to dwell at Shoukang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the empress dowager reached Zhongdu; Hailing led the officials to welcome her outside the city, and she took up residence at Shoukang Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，海陵及后宮、宰臣以下奉觴上壽，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: That day Hailing, the inner palace, and ministers down to the lowest rank raised cups to wish long life; they made merry to the utmost and then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Hailing, the inner palace, and all the ministers raised cups to wish her long life, feasted to their hearts' content, and then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 海陵侍太后于宮中，外極恭順，太后坐起，自扶腋之，常從輿輦徒行，太后所御物或自執之。

translations.literal: Hailing attended the empress dowager in the palace; outwardly he was extremely respectful and compliant. When the empress dowager sat or rose, he himself supported her under the arms; he often followed the carriage on foot; things the empress dowager used he sometimes carried himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing attended the empress dowager in the palace with outward show of utmost deference: when she sat or rose he supported her himself, often walked beside her carriage, and sometimes carried her belongings with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 見者以為至孝，太后亦以為誠然。

translations.literal: Those who saw it thought this utmost filial piety; the empress dowager also thought it sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers took this for perfect filial piety, and the empress dowager believed it sincere as well.

sentences.zh: 及謀伐宋，太后諫止之，海陵心中益不悅，每謁太后還，必忿怒，人不知其所以。

translations.literal: When he plotted to attack Song, the empress dowager admonished and tried to stop him; Hailing grew ever more displeased in heart; whenever he returned from paying court to the empress dowager he was always angry, and people did not know why.
translations.idiomatic: When he planned to attack Song, the empress dowager urged him to desist; Hailing grew ever more resentful and, after each visit to her, returned in a fury for reasons no one could fathom.

sentences.zh: 及至汴京，太后居甯德宮。

translations.literal: When they reached Bianjing, the empress dowager dwelt at Ningde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Bianjing, the empress dowager took up residence at Ningde Palace.

sentences.zh: 太后使侍婢高福娘問海陵起居，海陵幸之，因使伺太后動靜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent her serving maid Gaofuniang to inquire after Hailing's health; Hailing favored her and therefore had her spy on the empress dowager's movements.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent her maid Gaofuniang to inquire after Hailing's health; he took her to his bed and used her to spy on the empress dowager's every move.

sentences.zh: 凡太后動止，事無大小，福娘夫特末哥教福娘增飾其言以告海陵。

translations.literal: Whatever the empress dowager's movements, matters great or small, Gaofuniang's husband Temuge taught Gaofuniang to embellish her words in reporting to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the empress dowager did, great or small, Gaofuniang's husband Temuge taught her to embellish her reports to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 及樞密使僕散師恭征契丹撒八，辭謁太后，太后與師恭語久之。

translations.literal: When Privy Councilor Pusan Shigong campaigned against the Khitan Saba, he took leave to pay court to the empress dowager; the empress dowager spoke with Shigong for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Privy Councilor Pusan Shigong set out against the Khitan rebel Saba, he took leave of the empress dowager, and she spoke with him at length.

sentences.zh: 大概言「國家世居上京，既徙中都，又自中都至汴，今又興兵涉江、淮伐宋，疲弊中國，我嘗諫止之，不見聽。

translations.literal: In general she said: "The state has dwelt at Shangjing for generations; we already moved to Zhongdu, then from Zhongdu to Bian; now again we raise troops to cross the Yangtze and Huai to attack Song, exhausting China—I once admonished and tried to stop this, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In substance she said, "Our house has dwelt at Shangjing for generations; we moved to Zhongdu, then from Zhongdu to Bian; now we raise troops to cross the Yangtze and Huai to attack Song and exhaust the realm. I urged him to stop, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 契丹事復如此，奈何」。

translations.literal: The Khitan affair is again like this—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Khitan affair is the same again—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 福娘以告海陵。

translations.literal: Gaofuniang reported this to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaofuniang reported this to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵意謂太后以充為子，充四子皆成立，恐師恭將兵在外，太后或有異圖。

translations.literal: Hailing thought the empress dowager regarded Chong as her son; Chong's four sons were all grown; he feared that with Shigong commanding troops abroad, the empress dowager might have some other design.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing suspected that because the empress dowager regarded Chong as her son and Chong's four sons were all grown, she might plot something while Shigong commanded troops abroad.

sentences.zh: 乃召點檢大懷忠、翰林待制斡論、尚衣局使虎特末、武庫直長習失使殺太后于甯德宮，命護衛高福、辭勒、浦速斡以兵士四十人從，且戒之曰：「汝等見太后，但言有詔，令太后跪受，即擊殺之，匆令艱苦。

translations.literal: He then summoned Inspector-General Dahuaizhong, Hanlin Attendant-Compiler Wolun, Director of the Wardrobe Bureau Hutemu, and Armory Duty Officer Xishi to kill the empress dowager at Ningde Palace; he ordered guards Gaofu, Cile, and Pusuwo to follow with forty soldiers, and admonished them: "When you see the empress dowager, only say there is an edict; order the empress dowager to kneel and receive it, then strike and kill her—do not let her suffer hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Inspector-General Dahuaizhong, Hanlin Attendant-Compiler Wolun, Director of the Wardrobe Bureau Hutemu, and Armory Duty Officer Xishi to kill the empress dowager at Ningde Palace, with guards Gaofu, Cile, and Pusuwo and forty soldiers. He warned them, "When you see the empress dowager, say only that there is an edict; have her kneel to receive it, then strike her dead at once—do not let her suffer.

sentences.zh: 太后同乳妹安特，多口必妄言，當令速死。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager's milk-sister Ante is talkative and will surely speak rashly—she should be made to die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Her milk-sister Ante is talkative and will surely speak out of turn—she must die quickly as well."

sentences.zh: 及指名太后左右數人，皆令殺之。

translations.literal: He also named several of the empress dowager's attendants and ordered them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also named several of the empress dowager's attendants and ordered them killed.

sentences.zh: 太后方樗浦，大懷忠等至，令太后跪受詔。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was playing pitch-pot; Dahuaizhong and the others arrived and ordered the empress dowager to kneel and receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was playing pitch-pot when Dahuaizhong and the others arrived and ordered her to kneel and receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 太后愕然，方下跪，虎特末從後擊之，僕而復起者再。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was startled; just as she knelt, Hutemu struck her from behind; she fell and rose again twice.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was startled and had just knelt when Hutemu struck her from behind; she fell and rose twice more before they finished her.

sentences.zh: 高福等縊殺之，年五十三。

translations.literal: Gaofu and the others strangled her; she was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Gaofu and the others strangled her. She was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 並殺安特及郡君白散、阿魯瓦、叉察，乳母南撒，侍女阿斯、斡裏保，甯德宮護衛溫蒂罕查刺，直長王家奴、撒八，小底忽沙等。

translations.literal: They also killed Ante and Ladies Baisan, Aluwa, and Chacha, wet-nurse Nansa, serving maids Asi and Wolibao, Ningde Palace guard Wendihan Zhaci, duty officers Wangjianu and Saba, and attendants Husha, among others.
translations.idiomatic: They also killed Ante, Ladies Baisan, Aluwa, and Chacha, wet-nurse Nansa, maids Asi and Wolibao, Ningde Palace guard Wendihan Zhaci, duty officers Wangjianu and Saba, and attendants Husha, among others.

sentences.zh: 海陵命焚太后于宮中，棄其骨于水。

translations.literal: Hailing ordered the empress dowager burned in the palace and her bones cast into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered her body burned in the palace and her bones thrown into the water.

sentences.zh: 並殺充之子檀奴、阿裏白、元奴，耶補兒邇匿，歸於世宗。

translations.literal: He also killed Chong's sons Tannu, Alibai, and Yuannu; Yebbu'er'erni was hidden away and came under Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Chong's sons Tannu, Alibai, and Yuannu; Yebbu'er'erni was hidden away and later came under Emperor Shizong's protection.

sentences.zh: 自軍中召師恭還，殺之。

translations.literal: He recalled Shigong from the army and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Shigong from the field and executed him.

sentences.zh: 及殺阿斯子孫、撒八二子、忽沙二子。

translations.literal: He also killed Asi's descendants, Saba's two sons, and Husha's two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Asi's descendants, Saba's two sons, and Husha's two sons.

sentences.zh: 封高福娘為鄖國夫人，以特末哥為澤州刺史。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Gaofuniang as Lady of the State of Yun and appointed Temuge prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Gaofuniang as Lady of Yun and appointed Temuge prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 海陵許福娘征南回以為妃，賜銀二千兩。

translations.literal: Hailing promised Gaofuniang that when she returned from the southern campaign she would be made a consort, and granted her two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing promised that when she returned from the southern campaign he would make Gaofuniang a consort and gave her two thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 敕戒特末哥：「無酗酒毆福娘，毆福娘必殺汝。」

translations.literal: An edict admonished Temuge: "Do not drink to excess and beat Gaofuniang; if you beat Gaofuniang, you will surely be killed."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an admonition to Temuge: "Stop drinking to excess and striking Gaofuniang—if you strike her again, I will have you killed."

sentences.zh: 大定間，諡徒單氏曰哀皇后，自澤州械特末哥、福娘至中都誅之。

translations.literal: During the Dading era, Tudian was posthumously honored as Empress Ai; Temuge and Gaofuniang were fettered at Ze Prefecture and brought to Zhongdu, where they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading reign Lady Tudian was posthumously named Empress Ai; Temuge and Gaofuniang were shackled in Ze Prefecture, brought to Zhongdu, and put to death.

sentences.zh: 其後貶海陵為庶人。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hailing was demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hailing was stripped of his imperial rank and reduced to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 宗斡去帝號，復封遼王，徒單氏降封遼王妃云。

translations.literal: Zonggan relinquished the imperial title and was again enfeoffed as Prince of Liao; Tudian was demoted and enfeoffed as Princess of Liao, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan gave up the imperial title and was reinstated as Prince of Liao, while Lady Tudian was demoted to Princess of Liao.

sentences.zh: 海陵母大氏

translations.literal: Hailing's mother, the Das
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da, Hailing's Mother

sentences.zh: 海陵母，大氏。

translations.literal: Hailing's mother was of the Da clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's mother was Lady Da.

sentences.zh: 天德二年正月，與徒單氏俱尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiande, she and Tudian were both honored as empress dowagers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Tiande she and Lady Tudian were both raised to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 大氏居永甯宮。

translations.literal: Lady Da resided at Yongning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da lived in Yongning Palace.

sentences.zh: 曾祖堅嗣贈司空，祖臣寶贈司徒，父昊天贈太尉、國公，兄興國奴贈開府儀同三司、衛國公。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Jiansi was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works; her grandfather Chenbao was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Education; her father Haotian was posthumously granted Grand Minister of War and Duke of the State; her elder brother Xingguonu was posthumously granted Grand Palace Officer with Palatial Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her forebears were posthumously ennobled in succession: great-grandfather Jiansi as Grand Minister of Works, grandfather Chenbao as Grand Minister of Education, father Haotian as Grand Minister of War and state duke, and elder brother Xingguonu as Grand Palace Officer of the first rank and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，昊天進封為王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Haotian was further enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: That November Haotian was promoted to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 三年正月十六日，海陵生日，宴宗室百官于武德殿。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the first month of the third year, Hailing's birthday, the imperial clan and all officials were feasted at Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the first month of the third year, Hailing's birthday, he held a banquet for the imperial clan and officials in Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 大氏歡甚，飲盡醉。

translations.literal: Lady Da was very merry and drank until utterly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da was in high spirits and drank herself into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 明日，海陵使中使奏曰：「太后春秋高，常日飲酒不過數杯，昨見飲酒沉醉。

translations.literal: The next day Hailing had a palace messenger report: "The empress dowager's years are advanced; on ordinary days she drinks no more than a few cups, yet yesterday I saw her drink until deeply intoxicated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hailing sent a palace messenger to report: "The empress dowager is advanced in years and usually drinks only a few cups, yet yesterday I saw her completely drunk.

sentences.zh: 兒為天子，固可樂，若聖體不和，則子心不安，其樂安在。

translations.literal: A son who is Son of Heaven may indeed rejoice, but if Her Sacred Person is unwell, then this son's heart is unsettled—where then is the joy?
translations.idiomatic: As Son of Heaven I have reason to rejoice, but if Your Majesty's health suffers, how can I be at ease—what joy is there in that?

sentences.zh: 至樂在心，不在酒也。」

translations.literal: The highest joy lies in the heart, not in wine."
translations.idiomatic: True joy comes from the heart, not from the cup."

sentences.zh: 及遷中都，永壽宮獨留上京，大氏常以為言。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Zhongdu, Yongshou Palace alone remained at Shangjing, and Lady Da often spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Zhongdu, Yongshou Palace was left behind at Shangjing alone, and Lady Da brought it up again and again.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年四月，大氏有疾，詔以錢十萬貫求方藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhenyuan, Lady Da fell ill; an edict offered one hundred thousand strings of cash to seek prescriptions and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhenyuan Lady Da fell ill, and the court offered one hundred thousand strings of cash for remedies.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，遺言海陵，當善事永壽宮。

translations.literal: When her illness became critical, she left a testament to Hailing that he should treat Yongshou Palace well.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness worsened she left Hailing a dying charge: he must treat Yongshou Palace with kindness.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，崩。

translations.literal: On wuyin day, she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day she died.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省：「應隨朝官至五月一日方治事。

translations.literal: An edict to the Department of State Affairs: "Officials who attend court should not resume affairs until the first day of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to the Department of State Affairs: "Officials who attend court are not to resume business until the first day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 中都自四月十九日為始，禁樂一月。

translations.literal: In Zhongdu, beginning from the nineteenth day of the fourth month, music was forbidden for one month.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdu music was banned for one month starting on the nineteenth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 外路自詔書到日後，官司三日不治事，禁樂一月，聲鐘七晝夜。」

translations.literal: In the outer circuits, from the day after the edict arrived, government offices were not to conduct affairs for three days; music was forbidden for one month; bells were rung for seven days and nights."
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, from the day after the edict arrived, offices would suspend business for three days, music would be banned for a month, and bells would toll day and night for seven days."

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，大祥，海陵率後宮奠哭于菆宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, at the great mourning rites, Hailing led the inner palace in offering libations and weeping at the temporary tomb palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan, at the second-anniversary mourning rites, Hailing led the inner palace to offer libations and weep at the temporary tomb.

sentences.zh: 海陵將遷山陵於大房山，故大氏猶在菆宮也。

translations.literal: Hailing was about to relocate the imperial tombs to Mount Dafang, and therefore Lady Da still remained at the temporary tomb palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was preparing to move the imperial tombs to Mount Dafang, so Lady Da's remains still lay in the temporary tomb.

sentences.zh: 九月，太祖、太宗、德宗梓宮至中都。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the coffins of Taizu, Taizong, and Dezong arrived at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the coffins of Taizu, Taizong, and Dezong reached Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 尊諡曰慈憲皇后。

translations.literal: She was honored with the posthumous title Empress Cixian.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Empress Cixian, "Kind and Discerning."

sentences.zh: 海陵親行冊禮，與德宗合葬於大房山，升祔太廟。

translations.literal: Hailing personally performed the enfeoffment rite; she was buried together with Dezong on Mount Dafang and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing himself performed the enshrinement rite; she was buried with Dezong on Mount Dafang and given a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 大定七年，降封海陵太妃，削去皇后諡號。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dading, she was demoted and enfeoffed as Grand Consort of Hailing, and her empress posthumous title was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dading she was demoted to Grand Consort of Hailing and stripped of her empress posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 及宗幹降帝號，封遼王，詔徒童單氏為妃，而大氏與順妃李氏、甯妃蕭氏、文妃徒單氏並追降為遼王夫人。

translations.literal: When Zonggan relinquished the imperial title and was enfeoffed as Prince of Liao, an edict made Lady Tudian a consort; Lady Da, along with Shunfei Lady Li, Ningfei Lady Xiao, and Wenfei Lady Tudian, were all posthumously demoted to ladies of the Prince of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonggan gave up the imperial title and was made Prince of Liao, an edict named Lady Tudian his consort; Lady Da, along with Consorts Shun (Li), Ning (Xiao), and Wen (Tudian), were all retroactively demoted to ladies of the Prince of Liao.

sentences.zh: 海陵后徒單氏

translations.literal: Hailing's empress, Tudian
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian, Empress of Hailing

sentences.zh: 廢帝海陵后，徒單氏。

translations.literal: Empress of the deposed emperor Hailing, Tudian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudian, empress of the deposed emperor Hailing.

sentences.zh: 太師斜也之女。

translations.literal: Daughter of Grand Preceptor Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Grand Preceptor Xieye.

sentences.zh: 初為岐國妃，天德二年封為惠妃，九月，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At first she was consort of the State of Qi; in the second year of Tiande she was enfeoffed as Huifei; in the ninth month she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She had first been Consort of Qi; in the second year of Tiande she was made Lady of Grace, and in the ninth month she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月二十一日，后生日，百僚稱賀于武德殿。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month of the third year, the empress's birthday, the hundred officials offered congratulations at Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month of the third year, the empress's birthday, officials gathered at Wude Hall to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 久之，海陵后宮浸多，后寵頗衰，希得進見。

translations.literal: After a long time, Hailing's inner palace gradually grew numerous; the empress's favor declined considerably, and she rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: In time Hailing's harem grew ever larger; the empress lost much of his favor and seldom saw him.

sentences.zh: 沈璋妻張氏嘗為光英保母，耶律徹在北京與海陵遊從，海陵使璋妻及徹妻侯氏入宮侍后。

translations.literal: Shen Zhang's wife Lady Zhang had once been Guangying's nurse; Yelü Che in Beijing associated with Hailing in his leisure; Hailing had Zhang's wife and Che's wife Lady Hou enter the palace to attend the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang's wife Lady Zhang had once nursed Guangying; Yelü Che had kept company with Hailing in Beijing, and Hailing sent Zhang's wife and Che's wife Lady Hou into the palace to attend the empress.

sentences.zh: 徹本名神涅，負官錢二千六百餘萬，海陵皆免之。

translations.literal: Che's original name was Shennie; he owed official funds of more than twenty-six million, and Hailing remitted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Che's original name was Shennie; he owed more than twenty-six million in official debts, and Hailing forgave them all.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，海陵幸南京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, Hailing visited Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenglong Hailing traveled to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，左丞相張浩率百官迎謁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on guihai day, Left Chancellor Zhang Hao led the hundred officials in welcoming and paying respects.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the sixth month Left Chancellor Zhang Hao led the officials out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 海陵備法駕，乘玉輅，與后及太子光英共載而入。

translations.literal: Hailing prepared the imperial regalia, rode the jade carriage, and entered together with the empress and Crown Prince Guangying in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing came in full imperial regalia aboard the jade carriage, sharing it with the empress and Crown Prince Guangying as they entered the city.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，后與光英居守。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, the empress and Guangying remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing marched against Song, the empress and Guangying stayed behind to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 海陵遇害，陀滿訛裏也殺光英於汴。

translations.literal: When Hailing met with calamity, Tuoman Elie killed Guangying at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing was assassinated, Tuoman Elie killed Guangying at Bian.

sentences.zh: 后至中都，居於海陵母大氏故宮。

translations.literal: The empress arrived at Zhongdu and resided in the former palace of Hailing's mother Lady Da.
translations.idiomatic: The empress returned to Zhongdu and took up residence in the former palace of Hailing's mother, Lady Da.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世宗憐其無依，詔歸父母家于上京，歲賜錢二千貫，奴婢皆給官廩。

translations.literal: Before long, Shizong pitied her for having no support; an edict returned her to her parents' home at Shangjing, granting two thousand strings of cash annually; slaves and maid servants were all supplied from official stores.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shizong, pitying her isolation, ordered her home to her parents in Shangjing, granting her two thousand strings of cash each year and provisioning her servants from the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 大定十年卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dading she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the tenth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 海陵諸嬖附

translations.literal: Hailing's favored followers, appended
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Hailing's Favored Consorts

sentences.zh: 海陵為人善飾詐，初為宰相，妾媵不過三數人。

translations.literal: Hailing as a man was skilled at disguising deceit; when he first served as chancellor, his concubines and secondary wives numbered no more than three or so.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was a master of dissimulation; as chancellor his household held only two or three concubines.

sentences.zh: 及踐大位，逞欲無厭，后宮諸妃十二位，又有昭儀至充媛九位，婕妤美人才人三位，殿直最下，其他不可舉數。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the throne, he indulged his desires without limit: twelve consorts in the inner palace, plus nine ranks from Zhaoyi to Chongyuan, three of Jieyu, Meiren, and Cairen; palace attendants lowest of all—others beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the throne he indulged himself without restraint: twelve principal consorts, nine ranks from Lady of Bright Deportment down to Filled Beauty, three ranks of Jieyu, Beautiful Lady, and Talented Lady, and countless palace attendants below them.

sentences.zh: 初即位，封岐國妃徒單氏為惠妃，後為皇后。

translations.literal: Upon first taking the throne, he enfeoffed Consort of Qi Tudian as Huifei, later making her empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the throne he made Consort of Qi Lady Tudian Lady of Grace, and later empress.

sentences.zh: 第二娘子大氏封貴妃，第三娘子蕭氏封昭容，耶律氏封修容。

translations.literal: The second lady, Lady Da, was enfeoffed as Guifei; the third lady, Lady Xiao, as Zhaorong; Lady Yelü as Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: His second lady, Lady Da, was made Noble Consort; the third, Lady Xiao, was made Lady of Courtly Demeanor; and Lady Yelü was made Lady of Cultivated Demeanor.

sentences.zh: 其後貴妃大氏進封惠妃，貞元元年，進封姝妃，正隆二年，進封元妃。

translations.literal: Thereafter Noble Consort Lady Da was promoted to Huifei; in the first year of Zhenyuan, promoted to Shufei; in the second year of Zhenglong, promoted to Yuanfei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da was later promoted from Noble Consort to Lady of Grace, then in the first year of Zhenyuan to Lady of Graceful Beauty, and in the second year of Zhenglong to Primary Consort.

sentences.zh: 昭容蕭氏，天德二年，特封淑妃，貞元二年，進封宸妃。

translations.literal: Zhaorong Lady Xiao, in the second year of Tiande was specially enfeoffed as Shufei; in the second year of Zhenyuan, promoted to Chenfei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao, Lady of Courtly Demeanor, was made Lady of Gentle Grace in the second year of Tiande and promoted to Lady of the Inner Court in the second year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 修容耶律氏，天德四年，進昭媛，貞元元年，進昭儀，三年，進封麗妃。

translations.literal: Xiurong Lady Yelü, in the fourth year of Tiande was promoted to Zhaoyuan; in the first year of Zhenyuan, promoted to Zhaoyi; in the third year, promoted and enfeoffed as Lifei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yelü, Lady of Cultivated Demeanor, rose to Bright Beauty in the fourth year of Tiande, to Lady of Bright Deportment in the first year of Zhenyuan, and to Lady of Loveliness in the third year.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，後宮止此三人，尊卑之敘，等威之辨，若有可觀者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his reign the inner palace had only these three; the order of honor and distinction of rank and authority had something to be seen in it.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset his harem held only these three women, and the hierarchy of rank and precedence still had something respectable about it.

sentences.zh: 及其侈心既萌淫肆蠱惑，不可復振矣。

translations.literal: Once his extravagant heart had sprouted, dissolute seduction took hold, and it could no longer be restored.
translations.idiomatic: But once his appetite for excess took hold, debauchery and enticement ran unchecked, and order could never be restored.

sentences.zh: 昭妃阿裏虎，姓蒲察氏，駙馬都尉沒裏野女。

translations.literal: Zhaofei Aligu, surname Pucha, daughter of Commandant of Horse-Guards Moliye.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Aligu, Lady of Brightness, of the Pucha clan, was the daughter of Commandant of Horse-Guards Moliye.

sentences.zh: 初嫁宗盤子阿虎迭。

translations.literal: At first she married Zongpan's son Ahudie.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to Ahudie, son of Zongpan.

sentences.zh: 阿虎迭誅，再嫁宗室南家。

translations.literal: When Ahudie was executed, she remarried the clansman Nanjia.
translations.idiomatic: After Ahudie was executed she remarried Nanjia, a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 南家死，是時南家父突葛速為元帥都監，在南京，海陵亦從梁王宗弼在南京，欲取阿裏虎，突葛速不從，遂止。

translations.literal: When Nanjia died, at that time Nanjia's father Tugesu was marshal director stationed at Nanjing; Hailing also followed Prince of Liang Zongbi at Nanjing and wished to take Aligu; Tugesu would not consent, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjia died his father Tugesu was marshal director at Nanjing; Hailing was there with Prince of Liang Zongbi and wanted to take Aligu, but Tugesu refused and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 及篡位方三日，詔遣阿裏虎歸父母家。

translations.literal: When he had usurped the throne for only three days, an edict sent Aligu back to her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: Only three days after seizing the throne he ordered Aligu sent back to her parents.

sentences.zh: 閱兩月，以婚禮納之。

translations.literal: After two months had passed, he took her in with wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he took her into the palace with full wedding rites.

sentences.zh: 數月，特封賢妃，再封昭妃。

translations.literal: Within months she was specially enfeoffed as Xianfei, then again as Zhaofei.
translations.idiomatic: Within months she was made Lady of Virtue, then Lady of Brightness.

sentences.zh: 阿裏虎嗜酒，海陵責讓之，不聽，由是寵衰。
