translations.literal: Aligu was fond of wine; Hailing reproached and rebuked her, but she would not listen; thereby her favor declined.
translations.idiomatic: Aligu drank heavily; Hailing rebuked her, but she paid no heed, and his favor waned.

sentences.zh: 昭妃初嫁阿虎迭，生女重節。

translations.literal: When Zhaofei first married Ahudie, she bore a daughter, Chongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Aligu first married Ahudie she bore a daughter named Chongjie.

sentences.zh: 海陵與重節亂，阿裏虎怒重節，批其頰，頗有詆訾之言。

translations.literal: Hailing had illicit relations with Chongjie; Aligu was angry at Chongjie, slapped her cheek, and spoke words of considerable slander.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing took Chongjie as his lover; Aligu flew into a rage, struck her daughter's face, and hurled bitter insults.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞之，愈不悅。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard of it, he was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing heard of it and grew even angrier.

sentences.zh: 阿裏虎以衣服遺前夫之子，海陵將殺之，徒單后率諸妃嬪求哀，乃得免。

translations.literal: Aligu gave clothing to her former husband's son; Hailing was about to kill her; Empress Tudian led the consorts and concubines in begging for mercy, and she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Aligu gave clothes to her former husband's son, Hailing nearly had her killed; Empress Tudian led the consorts in pleading for her life, and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 凡諸妃位皆以侍女服男子衣冠，號「假廝兒」。

translations.literal: All consorts of rank had their serving women wear men's robes and caps, called "false lads."
translations.idiomatic: Every ranked consort dressed her maids in men's robes and caps, calling them "false lads."

sentences.zh: 有勝哥者，阿裏虎與之同臥起，如夫婦。

translations.literal: There was one called Shengge; Aligu slept and rose with her as man and wife.
translations.idiomatic: One maid named Shengge lived with Aligu as husband and wife, sharing bed and board.

sentences.zh: 廚婢三娘以告海陵，海陵不以為過，惟戒阿裏虎勿笞箠三娘。

translations.literal: The kitchen maid Sanniang reported this to Hailing; Hailing did not regard it as fault, only admonishing Aligu not to whip and beat Sanniang.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen maid Sanniang told Hailing; he saw no crime in it and merely warned Aligu not to beat Sanniang.

sentences.zh: 阿裏虎榜殺之。

translations.literal: Aligu had her beaten to death with the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Aligu had her beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞昭妃閤有死者，意度是三娘，曰：「若果爾，吾必殺阿裏虎。」

translations.literal: Hailing heard that someone had died in Zhaofei's quarters and guessed it was Sanniang; he said: "If it is indeed so, I will surely kill Aligu."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that someone had died in Lady Aligu's quarters, Hailing guessed it was Sanniang and said, "If that is so, I will kill Aligu."

sentences.zh: 問之，果然。

translations.literal: On inquiry, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked, it proved true.

sentences.zh: 是月，光英生月，海陵私忌，不行戮。

translations.literal: That month was Guangying's birth month; Hailing privately observed the taboo and did not carry out execution.
translations.idiomatic: That month was Guangying's birth month, and out of personal taboo Hailing withheld the execution.

sentences.zh: 阿裏虎聞海陵將殺之也，即不食，日焚香禱祝，冀脫死。

translations.literal: Aligu heard that Hailing was about to kill her; she at once stopped eating, burning incense daily in prayer, hoping to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Hailing meant to kill her, Aligu stopped eating and burned incense daily, praying to be spared.

sentences.zh: 逾月，阿裏虎已委頓不知所為，海陵使人縊殺之，並殺侍婢擊三娘者。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Aligu was already wasted and at a loss; Hailing sent men to strangle her to death, and also killed the serving maid who had beaten Sanniang.
translations.idiomatic: After a month Aligu was wasted and helpless; Hailing had her strangled and also killed the maid who had beaten Sanniang.

sentences.zh: 貴妃定哥，姓唐括氏。

translations.literal: Guifei Dingge, surname Tangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Dingge, of the Tangguo clan.

sentences.zh: 有容色。

translations.literal: She had fine appearance.
translations.idiomatic: She was beautiful.

sentences.zh: 崇義節度使烏帶之妻。

translations.literal: Wife of Chongyi Military Commissioner Wudai.
translations.idiomatic: She was the wife of Wudai, military commissioner of Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 海陵舊嘗有私，侍婢貴哥與知之幔烏帶在鎮，每遇元會生辰，使家奴葛魯、葛溫詣闕上壽，定哥亦使貴哥候問海陵及兩宮太后起居。

translations.literal: Hailing had once had a private affair; the serving maid Guige knew of it. Wudai was stationed at his post; whenever New Year's court or birthdays came, he sent household slaves Gelu and Gewen to the capital to offer longevity greetings; Dingge also sent Guige to inquire after Hailing and the two palaces of empress dowagers' health.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing and she had once been lovers, and her maid Guige knew it. While Wudai was away at his post, he sent household slaves Gelu and Gewen to court on holidays and birthdays to offer congratulations; Dingge likewise sent Guige to inquire after Hailing and both empress dowagers.

sentences.zh: 海陵因貴哥傳語定哥曰：「自古天子亦有兩后者，能殺汝夫以從我乎？」

translations.literal: Hailing through Guige conveyed words to Dingge: "Since antiquity Son of Heaven has also had two empresses—can you kill your husband to follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: Through Guige Hailing sent Dingge a message: "Even emperors of old had two empresses—will you kill your husband and come to me?"

sentences.zh: 貴哥歸，具以海陵言告定哥。

translations.literal: Guige returned and fully reported Hailing's words to Dingge.
translations.idiomatic: Guige returned and told Dingge everything Hailing had said.

sentences.zh: 定哥曰：「少時醜惡，事已可恥。

translations.literal: Dingge said: "In youth it was ugly and vile; the matter is already shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Dingge replied, "What happened in our youth was shameful enough as it is.

sentences.zh: 今兒女已成立，豈可為此。」

translations.literal: Now my children are grown—how could I do this?"
translations.idiomatic: My children are grown now—I cannot do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 海陵聞之，使謂定哥：「汝不忍殺汝夫，我將族滅汝家。」

translations.literal: When Hailing heard, he sent to tell Dingge: "If you cannot bear to kill your husband, I will exterminate your entire clan."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing heard this he sent word: "If you will not kill your husband, I will wipe out your whole family."

sentences.zh: 定哥大恐，乃以子烏荅補為辭，曰：「彼常侍其父，不得便。」

translations.literal: Dingge was greatly terrified and used her son Wudabu as an excuse, saying: "He constantly attends his father and there is no opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Dingge pleaded that her son Wudabu always attended his father and there was no chance."

sentences.zh: 海陵即召烏荅補為符寶祗候。

translations.literal: Hailing at once summoned Wudabu to serve as Keeper of the Seal and Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing immediately summoned Wudabu to court as Keeper of the Seal and Regalia.

sentences.zh: 定哥曰：「事不可止矣。」

translations.literal: Dingge said: "The matter cannot be stopped now."
translations.idiomatic: Dingge said, "There is no turning back now."

sentences.zh: 因烏帶醉酒，令葛溫、葛魯縊殺烏帶，天德四年七月也。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of Wudai's drunkenness, she had Gewen and Gelu strangle Wudai to death—it was the seventh month of the fourth year of Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: While Wudai was drunk she had Gewen and Gelu strangle him—it was the seventh month of the fourth year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞烏帶死，詐為哀傷。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard Wudai was dead, he feigned grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing learned Wudai was dead he pretended to mourn.

sentences.zh: 已葬烏帶，即納定哥宮中為娘子。

translations.literal: Once Wudai was buried, he at once took Dingge into the palace as a lady.
translations.idiomatic: After Wudai was buried he brought Dingge into the palace as a lady of rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，封為貴妃，大愛幸，許以為后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan she was enfeoffed as Guifei, greatly favored, with promise to make her empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan he made her Noble Consort, favored her deeply, and promised to make her empress.

sentences.zh: 每同輦游瑤池，諸妃步從之。

translations.literal: Each time he toured Jade Pool in the same carriage, the various consorts followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He often took her out in the imperial carriage to tour Jade Pool while the other consorts walked behind.

sentences.zh: 海陵嬖寵愈多，定哥希得見。

translations.literal: Hailing's favored attachments grew ever more numerous; Dingge rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: As Hailing's favorites multiplied, Dingge seldom saw him.

sentences.zh: 一日獨居樓上，海陵與他妃同輦從樓下過，定哥望見，號呼求去，詛罵海陵，海陵陽為不聞而去。

translations.literal: One day she was alone on an upper floor; Hailing passed below in the same carriage with another consort; Dingge saw them, cried out begging to go with them, cursed and reviled Hailing; Hailing pretended not to hear and went on.
translations.idiomatic: One day, alone upstairs, she saw Hailing pass below in his carriage with another consort; she cried out to be taken along and cursed him, but Hailing feigned not to hear and drove on.

sentences.zh: 定哥自其夫時，與家奴閻乞兒通，嘗以衣服遺乞兒。

translations.literal: Since the time of her husband, Dingge had illicit relations with the household slave Yan Qier and once gave clothing to Qier.
translations.idiomatic: Even while her husband lived Dingge had carried on with the household slave Yan Qier and had given him clothes.

sentences.zh: 及為貴妃，乞兒以妃家舊人，給事本位。

translations.literal: When she became Guifei, Qier as an old retainer of the consort's household was assigned to serve her quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After she became Noble Consort, Qier as a former member of her household was assigned to her service.

sentences.zh: 定哥既怨海陵疏己，欲復與乞兒通。

translations.literal: Dingge, resenting that Hailing had grown distant from her, wished to resume relations with Qier.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that Hailing had grown distant, Dingge wanted to renew her affair with Qier.

sentences.zh: 有比丘尼三人出入宮中，定哥使比丘尼向乞兒索所遺衣服以調之。

translations.literal: There were three Buddhist nuns who came and went in the palace; Dingge had the nuns ask Qier for the clothing she had given him, to flirt with him.
translations.idiomatic: Three Buddhist nuns frequented the palace; Dingge sent them to ask Qier for the clothes she had given him, using the request as a flirtation.

sentences.zh: 乞兒識其意，笑曰：「妃今日富貴忘我耶。」

translations.literal: Qier understood her intent and laughed, saying: "Consort, now that you are rich and noble, have you forgotten me?
translations.idiomatic: Qier saw what she meant and laughed: "My lady—now that you are wealthy and exalted, have you forgotten me?

sentences.zh: 定哥欲以計納乞兒宮中，恐閽者索之，乃令侍兒以大篋盛褻衣其中，遣人載之入宮。

translations.literal: Dingge wished by a stratagem to bring Qier into the palace; fearing the gatekeepers would search, she had her maidservant fill a large chest with intimate garments, then sent someone carrying it into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Planning to smuggle Qier into the palace, Dingge feared a search at the gate; she had a maid pack a large chest with underwear and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 閽者索之，見篋中皆褻衣，固已悔懼。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers searched it; seeing only intimate garments in the chest, they were already filled with regret and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the gatekeepers inspected the chest and found only underwear inside, regret and alarm already seized them.

sentences.zh: 定哥使人詰責閽者曰：「我，天子妃。

translations.literal: Dingge sent someone to rebuke the gatekeepers, saying: "I am the Son of Heaven's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Dingge sent men to upbraid the gatekeepers: "I am the emperor's consort.

sentences.zh: 親體之衣，爾故玩視，何也？

translations.literal: Garments that touch my own body—you deliberately gaze at them for amusement; why?
translations.idiomatic: These are garments that touch my skin—why do you stare at them so brazenly?

sentences.zh: 我且奏之。」

translations.literal: I shall report this."
translations.idiomatic: I will report you for this."

sentences.zh: 閽者惶恐曰：「死罪。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers said in terror: "A capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers cried in terror, "It is a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 請後不敢。」

translations.literal: Please—hereafter we dare not."
translations.idiomatic: We beg forgiveness and will never dare again."

sentences.zh: 定哥乃使人以篋盛乞兒載入宮中，閽者果不敢復索。

translations.literal: Dingge then had someone bring Qier in a chest into the palace; the gatekeepers indeed did not dare search again.
translations.idiomatic: Dingge then had Qier loaded into the chest and brought inside; as expected, the gatekeepers no longer dared to search.

sentences.zh: 乞兒入宮十餘日，使衣婦人衣，雜諸宮婢，抵暮遣出。

translations.literal: Qier entered the palace for more than ten days; she had him wear women's clothes, mingle among the palace maids, and sent him out at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten days Qier remained in the palace dressed as a woman among the maidservants, sent out each evening at dusk.

sentences.zh: 貴哥以告海陵。

translations.literal: Guige reported it to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Guige told Hailing what had happened.

sentences.zh: 定哥縊死，乞兒及比丘尼三人皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Dingge hanged herself; Qier and the three Buddhist nuns all suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Dingge hanged herself; Qier and the three nuns were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 封貴哥莘國夫人。

translations.literal: Guige was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Guige was granted the title Lady of Xin State.

sentences.zh: 初，海陵既使定哥殺其夫烏帶，使小底藥師奴傳旨定哥，告以納之之意。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Hailing had made Dingge kill her husband Wudai, he sent the young attendant Yaoshinu to convey an edict to Dingge, informing her of his intent to take her in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Hailing had compelled Dingge to murder her husband Wudai, he sent the page Yaoshinu to deliver his command and tell her he meant to bring her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 藥師奴知定哥與閻乞兒有奸，定哥以奴婢十八口賂藥師奴使無言與乞兒私事。

translations.literal: Yaoshinu knew Dingge had illicit relations with Yan Qier; Dingge bribed Yaoshinu with eighteen slaves and servants to keep silent about her affair with Qier.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshinu knew of Dingge's affair with Yan Qier; she paid him off with eighteen household servants to keep quiet about it.

sentences.zh: 定哥敗，杖藥師奴百五十。

translations.literal: When Dingge's plot failed, Yaoshinu was beaten one hundred fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingge's scheme collapsed, Yaoshinu received a hundred and fifty strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 先是，藥師奴嘗盜玉帶當死，海陵釋其罪，逐去。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yaoshinu had once stolen a jade belt and deserved death; Hailing pardoned his crime and expelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshinu had once stolen a jade belt—a capital offense—but Hailing pardoned him and banished him instead.

sentences.zh: 及遷中都，復召為小底。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Zhongdu, he was again summoned back as a young attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Zhongdu, Hailing recalled him as a page once more.

sentences.zh: 及藥師奴既以匿定哥奸事被杖，後與秘書監文俱與靈壽縣主有奸，文杖二百除名，藥師奴當斬。

translations.literal: After Yaoshinu had been beaten for concealing Dingge's affair, he later committed adultery with the Princess of Lingshou together with Secretary Director Wen; Wen was beaten two hundred strokes and dismissed from office; Yaoshinu was liable for decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: After his beating for covering up Dingge's adultery, Yaoshinu was later caught in an affair with the Princess of Lingshou County, along with Secretary Director Wen; Wen received two hundred strokes and was stripped of rank, while Yaoshinu faced execution.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲杖之，謂近臣曰：「藥師奴于朕有功，再杖之即死矣。」

translations.literal: Hailing wished to beat him and said to close ministers: "Yaoshinu has rendered service to me; if beaten again he will die at once."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing wanted to beat him instead and told his close advisers, "Yaoshinu has served me well—another beating would kill him."

sentences.zh: 丞相李睹等執奏藥師奴於法不可恕，遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Du and others insistently memorialized that Yaoshinu could not be forgiven by law, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Du and others pressed their memorial: Yaoshinu was beyond mercy under the law, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 海陵以葛溫、葛魯為護衛，葛溫累官常安縣令，葛魯累官襄城縣令，大定初，皆除名。

translations.literal: Hailing used Gewen and Gelu as guards; Gewen rose through offices to magistrate of Chang'an County, Gelu to magistrate of Xiangcheng County; at the beginning of Dading, both were stripped of names.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing employed Gewen and Gelu as bodyguards; Gewen eventually became magistrate of Chang'an County and Gelu of Xiangcheng County, but in the early Dading era both were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 麗妃石哥者，定哥之妹，秘書監文之妻也。

translations.literal: Lovely Consort Shige was Dingge's younger sister and the wife of Secretary Director Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Lovely Consort Shige was Dingge's sister and the wife of Secretary Director Wen.

sentences.zh: 海陵私之，欲納宮中。

translations.literal: Hailing took her privately and wished to bring her into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had an affair with her and wanted her in the palace.

sentences.zh: 乃使文庶母按都瓜主文家。

translations.literal: He then sent Wen's stepmother Andugua to manage Wen's household.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wen's stepmother Andugua to take charge of the Wen household.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂按都瓜曰：「必出而婦，不然我將別有所行。」

translations.literal: Hailing said to Andugua: "You must send out your daughter-in-law; otherwise I shall act otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told Andugua, "You must turn your daughter-in-law over to me, or I will take other measures."

sentences.zh: 按都瓜以語文，文難之。

translations.literal: Andugua told Wen; Wen found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Andugua relayed this to Wen, who resisted.

sentences.zh: 按都瓜曰：「上謂別有所行，是欲殺汝也。

translations.literal: Andugua said: "When the emperor says he will act otherwise, he means to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: Andugua said, "When the emperor threatens other measures, he means to kill you.

sentences.zh: 豈以一妻殺其身乎。」

translations.literal: Would you lose your life over one wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Is one wife worth your life?"

sentences.zh: 文不得已，與石哥相持慟哭而訣。

translations.literal: Wen had no choice; he and Shige clasped each other, weeping bitterly in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Left with no choice, Wen and Shige embraced and wept their farewell.

sentences.zh: 是時，海陵遷都至中京，遣石哥至中都，俱納之。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing moved the capital to Central Capital; he sent Shige to Zhongdu and had her brought into the palace as well.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hailing had moved the court to Central Capital; he sent Shige to Zhongdu and took her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 海陵召文至便殿，使石哥穢談戲文以為笑。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned Wen to the informal hall and had Shige speak foully and mock Wen for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing summoned Wen to the side hall and made Shige taunt him with obscene talk for sport.

sentences.zh: 定哥死，遣石哥出宮。

translations.literal: When Dingge died, he sent Shige out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingge's death, he sent Shige out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 不數日復召入，封為修容。

translations.literal: Within a few days he summoned her back and enfeoffed her as Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he recalled her and granted her the rank of Gentle Lady.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，進昭儀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, she was promoted to Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan she was promoted to Bright Consort.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，進封柔妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong, she was promoted and enfeoffed as Gentle Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenglong she was raised to Gentle Consort.

sentences.zh: 二年，進麗妃。

translations.literal: In the second year, she was promoted to Lovely Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The next year she was promoted to Lovely Consort.

sentences.zh: 柔妃彌勒，姓耶律氏。

translations.literal: Gentle Consort Mile, surname Yelü.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle Consort Mile was of the Yelü clan.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，使禮部侍郎蕭拱取之於汴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, he sent Vice Minister of Rites Xiao Gong to fetch her from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he sent Vice Minister of Rites Xiao Gong to bring her from Bian.

sentences.zh: 過燕京，拱父仲恭為燕京留守，見彌勒身形非若處女者，歎曰：「上必以疑殺拱矣。」

translations.literal: Passing through Yanjing, Gong's father Zhonggong was Yanjing regent; seeing Mile's form was not like a maiden's, he sighed: "The emperor will surely kill Gong out of suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: In Yanjing, where Gong's father Zhonggong served as regent, he saw that Mile's figure was not that of a virgin and sighed, "The emperor will kill Gong on suspicion."

sentences.zh: 及入宮，果非處女，明日遣出宮。

translations.literal: After she entered the palace, she indeed was not a virgin; the next day she was sent out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once she entered the palace it proved she was no virgin; the next day she was expelled.

sentences.zh: 海陵心疑蕭拱，竟致之死。

translations.literal: Hailing suspected Xiao Gong in his heart and ultimately caused his death.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's suspicion of Xiao Gong ultimately cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 彌勒出宮數月，復召入，封為充媛，封其母張氏莘國夫人，伯母蘭陵郡君蕭氏為鞏國夫人。

translations.literal: Mile left the palace for several months, then was summoned back and enfeoffed as Chongyuan; her mother Lady Zhang was enfeoffed as Lady of Xin State, her father's elder brother's wife, Lady of Lanling Commandery of the Xiao clan, as Lady of Gong State.
translations.idiomatic: After months outside the palace Mile was recalled and made Lady of Full Grace; her mother Lady Zhang became Lady of Xin State, and her aunt, Lady Xiao of Lanling Commandery, Lady of Gong State.

sentences.zh: 蕭拱妻擇特懶，彌勒女兄也。

translations.literal: Xiao Gong's wife Zetelán was Mile's elder sister by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gong's wife Zetelán was Mile's elder half-sister.

sentences.zh: 海陵既奪文妻石哥，卻以擇特懶妻文。

translations.literal: Hailing having seized Wen's wife Shige, instead gave Zetelán to Wen as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Wen's wife Shige, Hailing gave him Zetelán in marriage instead.

sentences.zh: 既而詭以彌勒之召，召擇特懶入宮，亂之。

translations.literal: Afterwards, under pretense of Mile's summons, he summoned Zetelán into the palace and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: Later, using Mile's name as a pretext, he summoned Zetelán to the palace and raped her.

sentences.zh: 其後，彌勒進封柔妃云。

translations.literal: Afterwards, Mile was promoted and enfeoffed as Gentle Consort, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Mile was later raised to Gentle Consort.

sentences.zh: 修儀高氏，秉德弟糺裏妻也。

translations.literal: Worthy Lady of Cultivation Lady Gao was the wife of Jiuli, younger brother of Bingde.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Lady Gao was the wife of Jiuli, younger brother of Bingde.

sentences.zh: 海陵殺諸宗室，釋其婦女。

translations.literal: Hailing killed the various imperial clansmen and released their wives and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing executed members of the imperial clan, he spared their women.

sentences.zh: 宗本子莎魯刺妻、宗固子胡裏刺妻、胡失來妻及糺裏妻，皆欲納之宮中，諷宰相奏請行之。

translations.literal: Zongben's son Shaluchi's wife, Zonggu's son Hulici's wife, Husilai's wife, and Jiuli's wife—all he wished to take into the palace; he hinted that the chancellors should memorialize requesting it be done.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted Zongben's daughter-in-law Shaluchi, Zonggu's daughter-in-law Hulici, Husilai's wife, and Jiuli's wife in the palace, and hinted that his chancellors should petition for it.

sentences.zh: 使徒單貞諷蕭裕曰：「朕嗣續未廣，此党人婦女有朕中外親，納之宮中何如？」

translations.literal: He had Tudan Zhen hint to Xiao Yu: "My succession is not yet broad; among these faction members' women are my relatives inside and outside the clan—what of taking them into the palace?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tudan Zhen to sound out Xiao Yu: "My heirs are still few; some of these women's kin are my relatives—what if I brought them into the palace?"

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「近殺宗室，中外異議紛紜，奈何復為此邪。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "We have lately killed the imperial clansmen; inside and outside the court opinion is agitated—how can we do this again?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "We have just slaughtered the clan—court and country are in uproar. How can we do this again?"

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「吾固知裕不肯從。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "I already knew Yu would not comply."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "I knew Yu would refuse."

sentences.zh: 乃使貞自以己意諷裕，必欲裕等請其事。

translations.literal: He then had Zhen on his own hint to Yu in his own meaning, insisting that Yu and the others must request the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zhen press Yu in his own words, determined that Yu and the others would petition for it themselves.

sentences.zh: 貞謂裕曰：「上意已有所屬，公固止之，將成疾矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen said to Yu: "The emperor's intent already has its object; if you stubbornly oppose it, illness will develop."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told Yu, "The emperor's mind is set; if you keep blocking him, you'll make yourself sick."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「必不肯已，唯上擇焉。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "I certainly will not stop—let the emperor choose."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "I won't give in; let the emperor decide as he wills."

sentences.zh: 貞曰：「必欲公等白之。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "I must have you gentlemen report it plainly."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "You must put it in writing yourselves."

sentences.zh: 裕不得已，乃其奏，遂納之。

translations.literal: Yu had no choice; then they memorialized, and the women were taken in.
translations.idiomatic: At last Yu yielded, they submitted the memorial, and the women were brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，封高氏為修儀，加其父高耶魯瓦輔國上將軍，母完顏氏封密國夫人。

translations.literal: Before long, Lady Gao was enfeoffed as Worthy Lady of Cultivation; her father Gao Yelüwa was promoted to Supporter-of-the-State General-in-Chief; her mother of the Wanyan clan was enfeoffed as Lady of Mi State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lady Gao became Worthy Lady of Cultivation; her father Gao Yelüwa was made Supporter-of-the-State General-in-Chief, and her Wanyan mother Lady of Mi State.

sentences.zh: 高氏以家事訴於海陵。

translations.literal: Lady Gao complained to Hailing about a household matter.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao appealed to Hailing over a family grievance.

sentences.zh: 海陵自熙宗時悻見悼后幹政，心惡之，故自即位，不使母、后得預政事。

translations.literal: Since Xizong's time Hailing had resentfully witnessed Empress Dao's interference in government and hated it in his heart; therefore from his accession he did not allow mother or empress to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Xizong's reign Hailing had resented Empress Dao's meddling in government; from his own accession he barred mothers and empresses from politics.

sentences.zh: 於是，遣高氏還父母家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Lady Gao back to her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lady Gao back to her parents' house.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省，凡后妃有請于宰相者，收其使以聞。

translations.literal: He issued an edict the Secretariat: whenever empresses or consorts made requests of chancellors, seize their messengers and report.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to intercept and report any messenger sent by a consort to a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 昭媛察八，姓耶律氏。

translations.literal: Bright Lady of Grace Chaba, surname Yelü.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Lady Chaba was of the Yelü clan.

sentences.zh: 嘗許嫁奚人蕭堂古帶。

translations.literal: She had once been betrothed to the Xiren Xiao Tangguidai.
translations.idiomatic: She had once been promised to the Xiren Xiao Tangguidai.

sentences.zh: 海陵納之，封為昭媛。

translations.literal: Hailing took her in and enfeoffed her as Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing took her into the palace and made her Bright Lady of Grace.

sentences.zh: 堂古帶為護衛，察人使侍女習撚以軟金鵪鶉袋數枚遺之。

translations.literal: Tangguidai served as guard; Chaba sent her maidservant Xinian to give him several soft-gold quail pouches as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguidai served as a guard; Chaba sent her maid Xinian to give him several pouches of soft gold shaped like quails.

sentences.zh: 事覺。

translations.literal: The matter was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: The affair came to light.

sentences.zh: 是時，堂古帶謁告在河間驛，召問之。

translations.literal: At that time Tangguidai was on leave at Hejian Station; he was summoned and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguidai was then on leave at Hejian post station and was summoned for questioning.

sentences.zh: 堂古帶以實對，海陵釋其罪。

translations.literal: Tangguidai answered truthfully; Hailing released his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguidai told the truth, and Hailing pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 海陵登寶昌門樓，以察八徇諸后妃，手刃擊之，墮門下死，並誅侍女習撚。

translations.literal: Hailing ascended Baochang Gate tower, paraded Chaba before the various empresses and consorts, struck her with his own blade, and she fell beneath the gate and died; the maidservant Xinian was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing mounted Baochang Gate tower, displayed Chaba before the consorts, cut her down with his own hand, and she fell dead below; maid Xinian was executed too.

sentences.zh: 壽甯縣主什古，宋王宗望女也。

translations.literal: Princess of Shouning Commandery Shigu was the daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shigu of Shouning was daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 靜樂縣主蒲刺及習撚，梁王宗弼女也。

translations.literal: Princess of Jingle Commandery Puci and Xinian were daughters of Prince Liang Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Puci of Jingle and Xinian were daughters of Prince Liang Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 師姑兒，宗雋女也。

translations.literal: Shigu'er was the daughter of Zongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu'er was Zongjun's daughter.

sentences.zh: 皆從姊妹。

translations.literal: All were sororal cousins.
translations.idiomatic: All were female cousins.

sentences.zh: 混同郡君莎裏古真及其妹余都，太傅宗本女也，再從姊妹。

translations.literal: Lady of Huntong Commandery Shaliguzhen and her younger sister Yudu were daughters of Grand Tutor Zongben—second cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shaliguzhen of Huntong and her sister Yudu, daughters of Grand Tutor Zongben, were second cousins.

sentences.zh: 郕國夫人重節，宗磐女孫，再從兄之女。

translations.literal: Lady of the State of Cheng Chongjie was the granddaughter of Zongpan—a daughter of a second cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chongjie of Cheng State was Zongpan's granddaughter, a daughter of his second cousin.

sentences.zh: 及母大氏表兄張定安妻奈刺忽、麗妃妹蒲魯胡只，皆有夫，唯什古喪夫。

translations.literal: And Lady Da's cousin on her mother's side Zhang Ding'an's wife Naicihu, and Lovely Consort's younger sister Puluhuzhi—all had husbands; only Shigu was widowed.
translations.idiomatic: Naicihu, wife of Zhang Ding'an (cousin to Lady Da), and Lovely Consort's sister Puluhuzhi all had husbands; only Shigu was a widow.

sentences.zh: 海陵無所忌恥，使高師姑、內哥、阿古等傳達言語，皆與之私。

translations.literal: Hailing was without scruple or shame; he had Gao Shigu, Neige, Agu, and others convey messages—all had illicit relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was utterly shameless, using Gao Shigu, Neige, Agu, and others as go-betweens; he slept with them all.

sentences.zh: 凡妃主宗婦嘗私之者，皆分屬諸妃，出入位下。

translations.literal: All princesses and imperial clan wives with whom he had been intimate were each assigned to various consorts' quarters, entering and leaving beneath their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Every princess and clan wife he had taken was assigned to a consort's household, passing in and out of her quarters.

sentences.zh: 奈刺忽出入元妃位，蒲魯胡只出入麗妃位，莎裏古填、余都出入貴妃位，什古、重節出入昭妃位，蒲刺、師姑兒出入淑妃位。

translations.literal: Naicihu entered and left Primary Consort's quarters; Puluhuzhi, Lovely Consort's; Shaliguzhen and Yudu, Guifei's; Shigu and Chongjie, Zhaofei's; Puci and Shigu'er, Shufei's.
translations.idiomatic: Naicihu attended Primary Consort's quarters; Puluhuzhi, Lovely Consort's; Shaliguzhen and Yudu, Noble Consort's; Shigu and Chongjie, Bright Consort's; Puci and Shigu'er, Pure Consort's.

sentences.zh: 海陵使內哥召什古。

translations.literal: Hailing had Neige summon Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent Neige to summon Shigu.

sentences.zh: 先於暖位小殿置琴阮其中，然後召之。

translations.literal: First in the small hall of the warm quarters he placed zithers and ruan lutes therein, then summoned her.
translations.idiomatic: He first laid out zithers and ruan in a small warm chamber, then sent for her.

sentences.zh: 什古已色衰，常譏其衰老以為笑。

translations.literal: Shigu's beauty had already faded; he often mocked her aging as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's looks had faded; he often mocked her age for laughs.

sentences.zh: 唯習撚、莎裏古真最寵，恃勢笞決其夫。

translations.literal: Only Xinian and Shaliguzhen were most favored; relying on their power they beat and flogged their husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xinian and Shaliguzhen enjoyed the greatest favor and used their power to beat their husbands.

sentences.zh: 海陵使習撚夫稍喝押護衛直宿，莎裏古真夫撒速近侍局直宿。

translations.literal: Hailing had Xinian's husband Shaoha on guard duty in the guards corps, and Shaliguzhen's husband Sasu on duty in the close attendance bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing assigned Xinian's husband Shaoha to night duty in the guard corps and Shaliguzhen's husband Sasu to duty in the close-attendance bureau.

sentences.zh: 謂撒速曰：「爾妻年少，遇爾直宿，不可令宿于家，常令宿於妃位。」

translations.literal: He said to Sasu: "Your wife is young; when you are on night duty you must not let her stay at home—always have her stay at the consort's quarters."
translations.idiomatic: He told Sasu, "Your wife is young; when you're on night duty she mustn't sleep at home—keep her at the consort's quarters."

sentences.zh: 每召入，必親伺候廊下，立久，則坐于高師姑膝上。

translations.literal: Each time she was summoned in, he personally waited in the corridor below; standing long, he would then sit on Gao Shigu's lap.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he sent for her he waited personally in the corridor; if kept standing long, he would sit on Gao Shigu's lap.

sentences.zh: 高師姑曰：「天子何勞苦如此。」

translations.literal: Gao Shigu said: "Son of Heaven, why toil and suffer so?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shigu said, "Your Majesty, why exhaust yourself like this?"

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「我固以天子為易得耳。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "I indeed regard being Son of Heaven as easy to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Being emperor comes easily to me.

sentences.zh: 此等期會難得，乃可貴也。」

translations.literal: Such rendezvous are hard to obtain—that is what is precious."
translations.idiomatic: These stolen meetings are rare—that is what makes them precious."

sentences.zh: 每於臥內遍設地衣，倮逐以為戲。

translations.literal: Each time in the sleeping chamber he spread floor mats throughout and played naked chasing games.
translations.idiomatic: In the bedchamber he carpeted the floor and played chase games in the nude.

sentences.zh: 莎裏古真在外為淫泆。

translations.literal: Shaliguzhen was licentious and debauched outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shaliguzhen was conducting affairs outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞之大怒，謂莎裏古真曰：「爾愛貴官，有貴如天子者乎。

translations.literal: Hailing heard and was greatly enraged; he said to Shaliguzhen: "You love noble officials—is any as noble as the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing flew into a rage and demanded of Shaliguzhen, "You fancy high officials—is anyone nobler than the emperor?

sentences.zh: 爾愛人才，有才兼文武似我者乎。

translations.literal: You love talent—is there talent combining civil and military like mine?
translations.idiomatic: You prize talent—is there anyone with my combined civil and military gifts?

sentences.zh: 爾愛娛樂，有豐富偉岸過於我者乎。」

translations.literal: You love pleasure—is there anyone richer, grander, and more imposing than I?"
translations.idiomatic: You chase pleasure—is anyone richer, grander, or more imposing than I?"

sentences.zh: 怒甚，氣咽不能言。

translations.literal: Enraged, his breath choked and he could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His fury choked him speechless.

sentences.zh: 少頃，乃撫慰之曰：「無謂我聞知，便爾慚恧。

translations.literal: After a little while he comforted her, saying: "Do not think that because I have heard of it you must be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: After a moment he soothed her: "Don't be ashamed just because I found out.

sentences.zh: 遇燕會，當行立自如，無為眾所測度也，恐致非笑。」

translations.literal: When at banquets and gatherings, conduct yourself naturally in walking and standing; do not let the crowd measure and guess, lest ridicule follow."
translations.idiomatic: At feasts act naturally—don't let others read you and invite mockery."

sentences.zh: 後亦屢召入焉。

translations.literal: Afterwards he also repeatedly summoned her in.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to summon her often afterward.

sentences.zh: 余都，牌印松古刺妻也。

translations.literal: Yudu was the wife of Paiyin Songguci.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu was married to Paiyin Songguci.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗曰：「餘都貌雖不揚，而肌膚潔白可愛。」

translations.literal: Hailing once said: "Yudu's looks are not striking, but her skin is clean and white and lovable."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once remarked, "Yudu's face is plain, but her skin is fair and lovely."

sentences.zh: 蒲刺進封壽康公主，什古進封昭甯公主，莎裏古真進封壽陽縣主，重節進封蓬萊縣主。

translations.literal: Puci was advanced to Princess Shoukang; Shigu to Princess Zhaoning; Shaliguzhen to Princess of Shouyang commandery; Chongjie to Princess of Penglai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Puci was made Princess Shoukang, Shigu Princess Zhaoning, Shaliguzhen Princess of Shouyang, and Chongjie Princess of Penglai.

sentences.zh: 重節即昭妃蒲察氏所生，蒲察怒重節與海陵淫，批其頰，海陵怒蒲察氏，終殺之者也。

translations.literal: Chongjie was born to Bright Consort of the Puchas; Pucha was angry that Chongjie had relations with Hailing and struck her on the cheek—Hailing was angry at the Puchas and in the end killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjie was the daughter of Bright Consort Pucha; when Pucha struck Chongjie on the cheek for her affair with Hailing, Hailing's anger at Pucha ended in her execution.

sentences.zh: 凡宮人在外有夫者，皆分番出入。

translations.literal: All palace women who had husbands outside went in and out in rotating shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women with husbands outside the palace were allowed in and out only in rotating shifts.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲率意幸之，盡遣其夫往上京，婦人皆不聽出外。

translations.literal: Hailing wished to favor them at will; he sent all their husbands to Shangjing and would not let the women go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to take them at will, Hailing sent all their husbands to Shangjing and forbade the women to leave the palace.

sentences.zh: 常令教坊番直禁中，每幸婦人，必使奏樂，撤其幃帳，或使人說淫穢語於其前。

translations.literal: He often had the Music Bureau take rotating duty in the inner palace; whenever he favored a woman he would have music played, remove her curtains, or have someone speak obscene words before her.
translations.idiomatic: He kept musicians from the Music Bureau on rotating duty inside the palace; whenever he took a woman he ordered music, had her curtains removed, or had attendants speak obscenities in her presence.

sentences.zh: 嘗幸室女不得遂，使元妃以手左右之。

translations.literal: Once when he favored a maiden and could not succeed, he had the Primary Consort assist with her hands.
translations.idiomatic: Once, unable to succeed with a maiden, he had the Primary Consort assist him with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 或妃嬪列坐，輒率意淫亂，使共觀。

translations.literal: Sometimes when consorts sat in a row, he would indulge in licentious disorder at will and make them all watch together.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes with consorts seated in a row he would indulge in open debauchery and force them all to watch.

sentences.zh: 或令人效其形狀以為笑。

translations.literal: Sometimes he had people imitate their shapes for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he had attendants mimic their postures for amusement.

sentences.zh: 凡坐中有嬪御，海陵必自擲一物於地，使近侍環視之，他視者殺。

translations.literal: Whenever consorts were seated present, Hailing would himself throw an object to the ground and have close attendants surround and watch it; whoever looked elsewhere was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever consorts were present at a gathering, Hailing would throw something to the floor and order attendants to surround it; anyone who looked away was executed.

sentences.zh: 誡宮中給使男子，於妃嬪位舉首者刓其目。

translations.literal: He warned the men who served in the palace that whoever raised his head before a consort's seat would have his eyes gouged out.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that any male servant who raised his eyes toward a consort's seat would have his eyes put out.

sentences.zh: 出入不得獨行，便旋，須四人偕往，所司執刀監護，不由路者斬之。

translations.literal: Going in and out, they could not walk alone; even for relieving themselves four had to go together, the responsible office holding blades to guard them—whoever left the path was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Women could not go about alone; even to relieve themselves four had to go together under armed guard, and anyone who left the prescribed route was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 日入後，下階砌行者死，告者賞錢二百萬。

translations.literal: After sunset, whoever walked down the steps died; the informer was rewarded two million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: After sunset anyone who stepped down the stairs was put to death, and informers were rewarded two million cash.

sentences.zh: 男女倉猝誤相觸，先聲言者賞三品官，後言者死，齊言者皆釋之。

translations.literal: If men and women accidentally touched in haste, whoever spoke first was rewarded with a third-rank office, whoever spoke later died, and if both spoke together both were released.
translations.idiomatic: If a man and woman accidentally touched, whoever cried out first was rewarded with a third-rank post, whoever cried out second was killed, and if both cried out together both were spared.

sentences.zh: 女使辟懶有夫在外，海陵封以縣君，欲幸之，惡其有娠，飲以麝香水，躬自揉拉其腹，欲墮其胎。

translations.literal: The palace woman Pilan had a husband outside; Hailing enfeoffed her as Lady of a commandery and wished to favor her; hating that she was pregnant, he made her drink musk-scented water and personally kneaded and pulled her belly, wishing to abort the fetus.
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman Pilan had a husband outside; Hailing made her a commandery lady and wished to take her, but fearing her pregnancy he gave her musk-scented water and personally kneaded her belly to force a miscarriage.

sentences.zh: 辟懶乞哀，欲全性命，苟得乳免，當不舉。

translations.literal: Pilan begged for mercy, wishing to preserve her life; if she could nurse and be spared, she would not bear children.
translations.idiomatic: Pilan begged for her life, promising that if spared she would nurse but bear no more children.

sentences.zh: 海陵不顧，竟墮其胎。

translations.literal: Hailing paid no heed and in the end aborted her fetus.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ignored her pleas and forced the miscarriage.

sentences.zh: 蒲察阿虎迭女叉察，海陵姊慶宜公主所生，嫁秉德之弟特裏。

translations.literal: Pucha Aohudie's daughter Chacha, born to Hailing's elder sister Princess Qingyi, was married to Bingde's younger brother Teli.
translations.idiomatic: Chacha, daughter of Pucha Aohudie and Hailing's elder sister Princess Qingyi, was married to Bingde's younger brother Teli.

sentences.zh: 秉德誅，當連坐，太后使梧桐請於海陵，由是得免。

translations.literal: When Bingde was executed she should have been implicated by association; the empress dowager had Wutong plead with Hailing, and thus she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingde was executed she should have been punished as kin; the empress dowager had Wutong plead with Hailing, and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 海陵白太后欲納叉察。

translations.literal: Hailing told the empress dowager he wished to take Chacha.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told the empress dowager he wished to take Chacha into the palace.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「是兒始生，先帝親抱至吾家養之，至於成人。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "When this child was first born, the late emperor personally carried her to my home to raise her until she reached adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "When this child was born, the late emperor himself brought her to my house and raised her to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 帝雖舅，猶父也，不可。」

translations.literal: Though the emperor is her uncle, he is still like a father—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Though you are her uncle by marriage, you are still like a father to her—it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 其後，嫁宗至安達海之子乙刺補。

translations.literal: Later she was married to Zongzhi Andahai's son Yicibu.
translations.idiomatic: She was later married to Yicibu, son of Zongzhi Andahai.

sentences.zh: 海陵數使人諷乙刺補出之，因而納之。

translations.literal: Hailing several times sent people to hint that Yicibu should send her out, and thus took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing repeatedly pressured Yicibu to divorce her, then took her for himself.

sentences.zh: 叉察與完顏守誠有奸，守誠本名遏裏來，事覺，海陵殺守誠，太后為叉察求哀，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Chacha had an affair with Wanyan Shoucheng; Shoucheng's original name was Elilai; when the matter was discovered Hailing killed Shoucheng; the empress dowager pleaded for Chacha and she was released.
translations.idiomatic: Chacha had an affair with Wanyan Shoucheng, originally named Elilai; when it was discovered Hailing executed Shoucheng, but the empress dowager pleaded for Chacha and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 叉察家奴告叉察語涉不道，海陵自臨問，責叉察曰：「汝以守誠死詈我邪？」

translations.literal: Chacha's household slave reported that Chacha's words touched on treason; Hailing personally interrogated her and reproached Chacha: "Do you revile me because Shoucheng died?"
translations.idiomatic: A household slave reported that Chacha had spoken treasonously; Hailing interrogated her himself and demanded, "Are you cursing me because Shoucheng is dead?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then killed her.
translations.idiomatic: He then had her killed.

sentences.zh: 同判大宗正阿虎里妻浦速碗，元妃之妹，因入見元妃，海陵逼淫之。

translations.literal: Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Aohuli's wife Pusuguan, the Primary Consort's younger sister, because she entered to see the Primary Consort, Hailing forced and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: Pusuguan, wife of Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Aohuli and younger sister of the Primary Consort, was raped by Hailing when she came to visit her sister.

sentences.zh: 浦速碗自是不復入宮。

translations.literal: Pusuguan from then on never again entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pusuguan never entered the palace again.

sentences.zh: 世宗為濟南尹，海陵召夫人烏林荅氏。

translations.literal: When Shizong was Military Governor of Jinan, Hailing summoned Lady Ulindah.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizong was Military Governor of Jinan, Hailing summoned his wife Lady Ulindah to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夫人謂世宗曰：「我不行，上必殺王。

translations.literal: The lady said to Shizong: "If I do not go, the emperor will surely kill you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ulindah told Shizong, "If I refuse to go, the emperor will surely kill you.

sentences.zh: 我當自勉，不以相累也。」

translations.literal: I shall encourage myself and not let you be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: I will do my utmost and not let you suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 夫人行至良鄉自殺，是以世宗在位二十九年，不復立后焉。

translations.literal: When the lady reached Liangxiang she killed herself—therefore during Shizong's twenty-nine years on the throne he never again established an empress.
translations.idiomatic: She killed herself at Liangxiang on the way—which is why, throughout Shizong's twenty-nine-year reign, he never took another empress.
